rdfs:label: Accept
rdfs:comment: An indication that the actor accepts the object — typically a Follow request or invitation.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. The classic ActivityPub use is responding to a `Follow` to confirm the relationship. The `as:object` is what's being accepted (often another Activity). Pair with `Reject` for the negative response.

rdfs:label: Action
rdfs:comment: An action performed by a direct agent on a direct object — schema.org's analogue of an activity.
notes: Schema.org's action vocabulary — used heavily for `schema:potentialAction` declarations on websites ("this site supports SearchAction with these parameters"). For ActivityPub-style social actions, `urn:solid:Activity` is the right base; for PROV processes, `prov:Activity`. Pick by domain.

rdfs:label: Activity
rdfs:comment: An action taken by an actor — the base for Create, Like, Follow, Announce, etc.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Object`. Pair with `as:actor` (the agent performing it), `as:object` (what it's done to), `as:target`, `as:published`. Rarely typed directly — pick a subclass like `urn:solid:Like`, `urn:solid:Follow`, `urn:solid:Create`. For PROV-grade activity tracking with start/end times, use `prov:Activity`.

rdfs:label: Add
rdfs:comment: An activity in which the actor is adding the object to the target.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. The `as:object` is the thing being added; `as:target` is the collection or container it's being added to. Distinct from `Create` (which brings a new object into existence) — `Add` references an existing object and places it somewhere.

examples.title: Add a note to a favorites collection

rdfs:label: Agent
rdfs:comment: A thing that acts — person, organization, group, or software.
notes: Use when the actor could be non-human (a bot, a group, a service). Prefer `urn:solid:Person` when you know the actor is specifically a human.

rdfs:label: Announce
rdfs:comment: An activity in which the actor is calling the audience's attention to the object — a boost or repost.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. The ActivityPub primitive for boost / repost / share — distinct from `Like` (favorite without redistribution) and `Create` (publishing a new object). The `as:object` is the resource being amplified to the actor's audience.

rdfs:label: Answer
rdfs:comment: An answer to a Question — typically posted on Q&A sites or forums.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Comment`. Pair with `schema:parentItem` pointing at the `urn:solid:Question`. Distinct from a generic `Comment` (which can be on anything) and from AS `Note` (microblog post). Use schema's Q&A pair (`Question` + `Answer`) for SEO-rich Q&A markup.

jsonld.https://schema.org/text: Yes, ActivityPub supports it via Like activities.

rdfs:label: Application
rdfs:comment: An ActivityStreams actor representing a software application — a bot, service, or automated client.
notes: One of the AS actor types alongside `as:Person`, `as:Group`, `as:Organization`, `as:Service`. Use for non-human actors that are software (clients, bots, automation). For PROV-grade software-agent attribution, see `prov:SoftwareAgent`.

rdfs:label: Article
rdfs:comment: An article — a written work, typically published as part of a larger publication.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Document` (and schema:CreativeWork). Use for blog posts, news articles, papers. Pair with `urn:solid:headline`, `urn:solid:articleBody`, `urn:solid:author` for full schema.org-style modelling. For ActivityPub-style social posts, see `as:Article` or `as:Note`.

examples.title: A blog post as an Article

rdfs:label: Association
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV association — the role-aware participation of an Agent in an Activity.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:Attribution`: Association links Agent → Activity (who did the work), Attribution links Agent → Entity (who's responsible for the result). Carries `prov:agent`, `urn:solid:hadRole`, and `urn:solid:hadPlan`. Linked from an Activity via `prov:qualifiedAssociation`.

examples.title: Build run with a software-agent association

rdfs:label: Attribution
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV attribution — the role-aware relation between an Entity and the Agent it is attributed to.
notes: Use to qualify `prov:wasAttributedTo` with a role and timing. Linked from an Entity via `prov:qualifiedAttribution`. Carries `prov:agent` (the responsible Agent) and `urn:solid:hadRole` (the role they took — author, photographer, contributor).

rdfs:label: Audio
rdfs:comment: An audio resource — used in ActivityPub for audio attachments and stand-alone audio posts.
notes: ActivityStreams audio type — use for fediverse audio posts and attachments. Distinct from `urn:solid:AudioObject` (schema.org) which carries richer media metadata. Pick by data flavor: AS for ActivityPub-style social data, schema for SEO/structured-data web pages.

rdfs:label: AudioObject
rdfs:comment: An audio file with structured metadata — duration, encoding, transcript.
notes: Schema.org's audio type — podcasts, voice memos, sound effects. Carries `schema:contentUrl`, `schema:duration`, `schema:encodingFormat`, `schema:transcript`. For music tracks specifically, `schema:MusicRecording` adds artist/album fields.

rdfs:label: BasicContainer
rdfs:comment: An LDP Container whose membership is defined entirely by `ldp:contains` triples.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Container`. The default container shape used by Solid pods — every directory-like resource is typically a `BasicContainer` whose members are listed via `ldp:contains`. Use `ldp:DirectContainer` or `ldp:IndirectContainer` only when you need server-managed membership semantics.

examples.title: A pod root as a BasicContainer

rdfs:label: BibliographicResource
rdfs:comment: A book, article, or other documentary resource — typically with structured citation metadata.
notes: Library/archive-flavored class for the things a bibliography indexes — books, journal articles, conference papers, datasets. Pair with `urn:solid:bibliographicCitation`, `urn:solid:isPartOf` (linking article→issue→journal), and `urn:solid:identifier` (DOI, ISBN). For schema.org-flavored data, prefer specific subclasses like `urn:solid:Book` or `urn:solid:Article`.

jsonld.urn:solid:bibliographicCitation: Liddell, A. (2026). On Wonderlands. Solid Journal, 1(1), 1-10.

rdfs:label: Block
rdfs:comment: An indication that the actor is blocking the object — typically another actor.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. The `as:object` is the actor being blocked. By ActivityPub convention, Block activities should NOT be delivered to the blocked actor — receivers process them locally to filter out interactions. To unblock, send an `as:Undo` of the Block.

rdfs:label: BlogPosting
rdfs:comment: A single blog post — an entry in a weblog, typically with a date and an author.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Article`. Use specifically for blog entries when you want SEO/syndication semantics that distinguish them from news or scholarly articles. Pair with `schema:isPartOf` pointing at the parent `schema:Blog`.

rdfs:label: Book
rdfs:comment: A book — a long-form written work, typically published as a single physical or digital volume.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:CreativeWork`. Pair with `schema:isbn`, `schema:numberOfPages`, `schema:bookEdition`, `schema:author`. For audiobook or e-book editions specifically, schema.org provides `schema:Audiobook` and `schema:EBook` subclasses.

rdfs:label: Brand
rdfs:comment: A brand — a distinctive identity associated with a product, service, or organization.
notes: A Brand is a marketing identity, not the legal Organization that owns it — Pepsi (the brand) ≠ PepsiCo (the company). One Organization may own many Brands. Use `schema:brand` on a `urn:solid:Product` to link to its brand.

rdfs:label: Bundle
rdfs:comment: A named bundle of PROV provenance descriptions — a way to attribute provenance to provenance.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Entity`. A Bundle wraps a collection of PROV statements so they themselves can be the subject of further PROV — "who said this, when, why". Useful for distinguishing claims from different sources or for versioning provenance assertions.

examples.title: A bundle of provenance attributed to an agent

rdfs:label: Catalog
rdfs:comment: A DCAT Catalog — a curated collection of metadata about Datasets and DataServices.
notes: The container for an open-data portal or research-data repository. Members listed via `dcat:dataset` (datasets) and `dcat:service` (services). Pair with `dcterms:publisher`, `urn:solid:license`. The W3C DCAT 3 spec is the current normative reference.

rdfs:label: City
rdfs:comment: A city — a permanent settlement of significant size.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Place` (via `schema:AdministrativeArea`). Pair with `schema:containedInPlace` pointing at the containing `urn:solid:Country` to anchor it in the geographic hierarchy. For coordinates, attach `urn:solid:hasGeo`.

rdfs:label: Collection
rdfs:comment: An unordered collection of objects.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Object`. Use `as:items` (or paginate via `as:first`/`as:next`) to enumerate members. For ordered membership (timelines, replies, outboxes), use `as:OrderedCollection`. For Linked Data Platform containers with HTTP-level membership semantics, use `ldp:Container`.

rdfs:label: Comment
rdfs:comment: A comment on the parent CreativeWork — a reader's response or annotation.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:CreativeWork`. Schema.org's comment type is for blog/article comments; pair with `schema:parentItem` (or `urn:solid:inReplyTo` for AS-style threading). For ActivityPub microblog responses, prefer `urn:solid:Note` with `inReplyTo`.

rdfs:label: Communication
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV communication — the role-aware form of `wasInformedBy` between two Activities.
notes: Use to qualify a `prov:wasInformedBy` with role and timing. Linked from an Activity via `prov:qualifiedCommunication`. Carries `prov:activity` (the prior Activity) and optional `urn:solid:hadActivity`/`urn:solid:hadRole`. Rare in casual data — most uses of "this followed that" stay at the `wasInformedBy` level.

rdfs:label: Concept
rdfs:comment: A SKOS concept — a unit of thought (topic, category, term) suitable for use in a controlled vocabulary or thesaurus.
notes: The atom of SKOS — every entry in a thesaurus, taxonomy, or controlled vocabulary is a Concept. Pair with `urn:solid:prefLabel` (canonical name), `urn:solid:altLabel` (synonyms), `urn:solid:broader`/`urn:solid:narrower` (hierarchy), and `urn:solid:inScheme` (membership in a `ConceptScheme`).

examples.title: A concept in a tagging vocabulary

rdfs:label: ConceptScheme
rdfs:comment: A SKOS concept scheme — an aggregation of related Concepts, typically a thesaurus, taxonomy, or controlled vocabulary.
notes: The container for a controlled vocabulary. Concepts join via `urn:solid:inScheme`; the entry-point Concepts (no broader concept in this scheme) are listed via `urn:solid:hasTopConcept`. The IRI of the ConceptScheme itself is the canonical reference for the vocabulary as a whole.

rdfs:label: ContactPoint
rdfs:comment: A contact point for a person or organization — an aggregation of reachable contact channels for a specific purpose or department.
notes: Use to bundle multiple contact channels (email + phone + hours + language) under a single descriptive label like "customer support" or "press inquiries". For a vCard-style structured contact, the equivalent base is `vcard:VCard`.

rdfs:label: Container
rdfs:comment: A Linked Data Platform Container — an LDP resource that contains other resources, the LDP analogue of a directory.
notes: The base LDP container type. Solid pods organise data into Containers (typically `ldp:BasicContainer`); members are listed via `urn:solid:contains`. Distinct from `as:Collection`, which is a logical grouping at the data layer rather than an HTTP-level resource container.

examples.title: An LDP container with two members

rdfs:label: Country
rdfs:comment: A country — a sovereign nation-state or territory.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Place` (via `schema:AdministrativeArea`). Pair with an ISO 3166-1 country code via `schema:identifier` for machine-readability. For US states, EU countries, and other administrative regions, use `schema:City`, `schema:State`, or `schema:AdministrativeArea` accordingly.

examples.title: A country with an ISO code

rdfs:label: Create
rdfs:comment: An activity in which the actor has created the object.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. The canonical ActivityPub side-effect for publishing a new object — when an actor posts a Note, the wire-level activity is `Create` whose `as:object` is that Note. For PROV-grade generation events with timing, prefer `prov:wasGeneratedBy`.

rdfs:label: CreativeWork
rdfs:comment: The most generic kind of creative work — written, photographic, artistic, or otherwise.
notes: Schema.org's catch-all for authored content — books, movies, articles, photos, software, datasets. Subclasses include `urn:solid:Article`, `schema:Book`, `schema:Movie`. Pair with `urn:solid:creator`, `urn:solid:license`, `urn:solid:datePublished` for typical attribution metadata.

rdfs:label: DataService
rdfs:comment: A DCAT DataService — a service that gives access to one or more Datasets via an API or query interface.
notes: DCAT 2's class for SPARQL endpoints, REST APIs, OGC services, and other data-access services. Distinct from `urn:solid:Service` (the AS actor type for ActivityPub services). Pair with `dcat:endpointURL` and `dcat:servesDataset` to link the service to the Datasets it exposes.

examples.title: A SPARQL endpoint as a DataService

rdfs:label: Dataset
rdfs:comment: A DCAT Dataset — a collection of data, published or curated by a single agent and available in one or more representations.
notes: DCAT's central class for data publication. Represents the abstract dataset; concrete files/APIs serving its content are `urn:solid:Distribution`s. Pair with `dcterms:title`, `dcterms:description`, `dcterms:publisher`, `urn:solid:keywords`, `dcat:theme`. Schema.org's `schema:Dataset` is the SEO-flavored equivalent.

rdfs:label: Delegation
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV delegation — the role-aware form of `actedOnBehalfOf` between two Agents.
notes: Use to qualify a `prov:actedOnBehalfOf` with role and the activity it occurred during. Linked from a delegate Agent via `prov:qualifiedDelegation`. Useful for bots-on-behalf-of-users, services-acting-for-organizations.

rdfs:label: Delete
rdfs:comment: An activity in which the actor has deleted the object.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. The wire-level signal that an object has been removed. Receivers typically replace their cached object with an `as:Tombstone` rather than dropping the record entirely, preserving links from elsewhere.

rdfs:label: Derivation
rdfs:comment: A typed PROV derivation event — a relation between a derived entity and the entity it was derived from.
notes: Use to qualify a `prov:wasDerivedFrom` with role, generation, usage, or activity context (via `prov:qualifiedDerivation`). Specialized subclasses include `urn:solid:Revision` (substantive change), `urn:solid:Quotation` (excerpt), and `prov:PrimarySource` (first-hand origin).

rdfs:label: DirectContainer
rdfs:comment: An LDP Container that adds membership triples on a separate `membershipResource` rather than carrying them itself.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Container`. Use when membership of new resources should be reflected on a *different* resource — e.g. a comments container whose POSTs add triples to the parent article. Carries `ldp:membershipResource` and `ldp:hasMemberRelation` to define the relation. Most Solid pods use `urn:solid:BasicContainer` instead.

examples.title: A direct container reflecting members on its parent

rdfs:label: Distribution
rdfs:comment: A DCAT Distribution — a specific representation of a Dataset (a downloadable file or accessible API).
notes: One Dataset typically has multiple Distributions — CSV, JSON, RDF, API endpoint, archive. Pair with `urn:solid:downloadURL` (direct file URL), `urn:solid:accessURL` (general access page or API), `urn:solid:format`, `urn:solid:byteSize`. Linked from a Dataset via `dcat:distribution`.

rdfs:label: Document
rdfs:comment: A document of any kind — typically a web resource.
notes: Use as the type of any document-like resource (web page, file, blog post home). For richer creative-work modeling with authorship, dates, and licensing, `schema:CreativeWork` carries more fields. Note that `urn:solid:Image` is a subclass of Document.

rdfs:label: EducationalOrganization
rdfs:comment: An educational organization — a school, college, university, or training institute.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Organization`. Use as the value type of `urn:solid:alumniOf` for richer educational-history data than a bare `foaf:schoolHomepage` URL. Schema.org has narrower subclasses (`School`, `CollegeOrUniversity`, `HighSchool`, `MiddleSchool`) for specific levels.

rdfs:label: EmptyCollection
rdfs:comment: A PROV Collection with no members — the explicit empty case.
notes: Useful when you need to assert "this collection is definitively empty" rather than "the membership is unknown". Often the first state of a collection in a build pipeline before items are added; subsequent versions then `prov:wasDerivedFrom` the EmptyCollection.

rdfs:label: Entity
rdfs:comment: Anything in PROV that has provenance — a thing whose existence and history can be tracked.
notes: PROV's most general thing class — documents, datasets, software releases, physical objects can all be Entities. Used as the subject of `prov:wasGeneratedBy`, `prov:wasDerivedFrom`, `prov:wasAttributedTo`. Distinct from `as:Object` which is the ActivityStreams base class for social-graph objects.

examples.title: A versioned document as a PROV Entity

rdfs:label: Event
rdfs:comment: An event happening at a certain time and (often) location.
notes: Use for scheduled occurrences — meetings, conferences, releases, performances. Pair with `schema:startDate`, `schema:endDate`, `schema:location`. For ActivityStreams-style social events (with attendees as actors), `as:Event` carries actor-friendly semantics.

rdfs:label: FileFormat
rdfs:comment: A digital file format — typically referenced as the type of a `dcterms:format` value.
notes: Use as @type for FileFormat resources referenced from `urn:solid:format`. The IANA media type registry serves as the canonical FileFormat namespace; values typically come from there. For the broader "this is a media type" class, see `dcterms:MediaType`.

rdfs:label: Follow
rdfs:comment: An indication that the actor wants to follow the object — typically another Actor.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. The ActivityPub follow request — typically responded to with `as:Accept` or `as:Reject` by the followee. Use `urn:solid:knows` for non-directed acquaintance (FOAF tradition). To unfollow, send an `as:Undo` of the original Follow.

rdfs:label: FormalOrganization
rdfs:comment: An ORG FormalOrganization — an organization with legal recognition (company, government body, registered nonprofit).
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Organization`. Distinguishes legally-recognized entities from informal collectives (which stay at the `Organization` level). Use when legal status matters — contracts, regulatory filings, official records. Pair with `org:identifier` for the registration number.

rdfs:label: Frequency
rdfs:comment: A rate at which something recurs — daily, weekly, monthly, etc.
notes: Used to type Frequency values referenced by `dcterms:accrualPeriodicity` (the frequency at which a dataset is updated). Common controlled-vocabulary values come from the EU Publications Office Frequency vocabulary. For ad-hoc use, free-form strings are acceptable.

rdfs:label: Generation
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV generation event — the moment an Activity produced an Entity.
notes: Use to qualify `prov:wasGeneratedBy` with timing, role, or location. Linked from an Entity via `prov:qualifiedGeneration`. Carries `prov:activity`, `urn:solid:atTime`, and `urn:solid:hadRole`.

rdfs:label: GeoCoordinates
rdfs:comment: The geographic coordinates of a place — a latitude/longitude pair, optionally with elevation.
notes: Carries `schema:latitude` and `schema:longitude` (decimal degrees, WGS-84) and optional `schema:elevation`. Use as the value of `schema:geo` on a Place. For a `geo:` URI shortcut, see `urn:solid:hasGeo`. For shapes (polygons), use `schema:GeoShape`.

rdfs:label: Group
rdfs:comment: A collection of agents — informal or ad-hoc, not necessarily a formal organization.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Agent`. Use for any collection of agents — friends, mailing-list subscribers, project contributors. Use `urn:solid:Organization` when the collective has formal/legal structure. Members are listed with `urn:solid:member`.

rdfs:label: Image
rdfs:comment: An image — a document that is a still picture (PNG, JPEG, SVG, etc.).
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Document`. Use as the value type of `urn:solid:depiction` / `urn:solid:img`. For rich image metadata (dimensions, encoding, captions), `schema:ImageObject` carries more fields.

rdfs:label: ImageObject
rdfs:comment: A rich image object — an image with structured metadata like dimensions, encoding, and caption.
notes: Schema.org's metadata-rich image type. Use when you need fields like `schema:width`, `schema:height`, `schema:contentUrl`, `schema:caption`, `schema:encodingFormat`. For a bare image resource without those fields, `urn:solid:Image` (FOAF) is enough.

rdfs:label: IndirectContainer
rdfs:comment: An LDP Container whose membership triples reference an indirected member resource via `insertedContentRelation`.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Container`. The most flexible LDP container type — when a new resource is POSTed, the server uses `ldp:insertedContentRelation` to extract the value to use as the actual membership target. Useful for federated data where the resource POSTed isn't itself the subject of the membership triple. Rarely needed; most Solid pods use `urn:solid:BasicContainer`.

rdfs:label: Influence
rdfs:comment: PROV's most general qualified-relation superclass — any role-aware connection between an Activity, Entity, or Agent.
notes: Superclass of all PROV qualified relations (`Generation`, `Usage`, `Attribution`, `Association`, `Derivation`, `Communication`, `Delegation`, `Invalidation`, `End`, `Start`). Rarely typed directly — pick a specific subclass for clarity. Useful when reasoning generically over PROV qualifications.

rdfs:label: Invalidation
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV invalidation event — the moment an Entity ceased to exist.
notes: End-of-life counterpart to `urn:solid:Generation`. Use to qualify `prov:wasInvalidatedBy` with `urn:solid:atTime` and other context. Linked from an Entity via `prov:qualifiedInvalidation`. ActivityStreams' lighter equivalent for social data is `as:Tombstone`.

examples.title: Qualified invalidation of a deleted post

rdfs:label: ItemList
rdfs:comment: An ordered list of items — schema.org's lightweight ordered collection for SEO-rich markup.
notes: Schema.org's order-aware list type. Pair with `schema:itemListElement` (each item, optionally wrapped in `schema:ListItem` carrying `schema:position`). For ActivityStreams ordered collections, prefer `urn:solid:OrderedCollection`. Heavily used by SEO for top-N lists, breadcrumbs, FAQ pages.

rdfs:label: JobPosting
rdfs:comment: A listing for a job — an opportunity to be employed in a specific role.
notes: Pair with `schema:hiringOrganization`, `schema:jobLocation`, `schema:datePosted`, `schema:baseSalary`, `schema:employmentType`. Heavily used by job boards for SEO rich results — Google specifically rewards correct JobPosting markup.

rdfs:label: Jurisdiction
rdfs:comment: A legal, political, or administrative jurisdiction — a country, state, or governing region.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:Country`: a Jurisdiction can be sub-national (US state, EU directive area), supra-national (UN, EU), or non-geographic (corporate by-laws). Used in legal/regulatory metadata to scope which laws or rules apply.

rdfs:label: LicenseDocument
rdfs:comment: A legal document giving permission to do something with a resource — typically referenced by the `license` predicate.
notes: The class for license documents themselves — Creative Commons license pages, SPDX license texts, custom EULAs. Use as the `@type` of the resource pointed to by `urn:solid:license`. Existing well-known licenses (Creative Commons, SPDX) usually don't carry this type explicitly, but it's the formal class.

rdfs:label: Like
rdfs:comment: An indication that the actor likes, recommends, or favorites the object.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. The classic ActivityPub favourite/like. The `as:object` is the thing being liked; `as:actor` is the liker; `as:published` records when. To unlike, send an `as:Undo` of the original Like.

rdfs:label: LinguisticSystem
rdfs:comment: A system of communication including written, spoken, signed, or symbolic languages.
notes: Use as @type for resources representing languages — typically referenced from `urn:solid:language` when you need a structured Language resource rather than a bare BCP 47 tag. The IANA language subtag registry serves as the canonical LinguisticSystem namespace.

rdfs:label: Logo
rdfs:comment: A vCard Logo resource — the logo image associated with a vCard (typically for an Organization).
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:Photo` (typically a person's portrait) and generic `urn:solid:Image`: a Logo specifically represents a brand or organizational mark. Used as the value of `urn:solid:hasLogo`.

rdfs:label: MemberSubject
rdfs:comment: An LDP marker class for the special predicate value used by IndirectContainers when membership is computed from the inserted resource itself.
notes: Used as the value of `ldp:insertedContentRelation` to indicate "use the new resource itself as the membership target, not a property inside it". Niche LDP escape hatch — most use cases are better served by ldp:BasicContainer or by naming a specific predicate.

rdfs:label: Membership
rdfs:comment: An ORG Membership — a role-and-time-aware participation of an Agent in an Organization.
notes: Use when membership has structure — start/end dates, role, or compensation — that doesn't fit into a flat `urn:solid:memberOf` triple. Carries `org:member` (the Agent), `org:organization` (the Organization), and `org:role`. For simple membership, the flat `urn:solid:memberOf` predicate is enough.

rdfs:label: Move
rdfs:comment: An activity in which the actor moves the object from one location (origin) to another (target).
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. Combines `Add` + `Remove` semantics: `as:object` is what's being moved, `as:origin` names the source location, `as:target` names the destination. Common use in ActivityPub is account migration (moving an actor from one server to another).

rdfs:label: Movie
rdfs:comment: A movie — a feature-length motion picture released as a single work.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:CreativeWork`. Distinct from `urn:solid:VideoObject` — `Movie` is the work (the film as art), `VideoObject` is the file (a particular encoding). One Movie can have many VideoObject encodings. Pair with `schema:director`, `schema:actor`, `urn:solid:duration`.

examples.title: A movie with director and runtime

rdfs:label: MusicRecording
rdfs:comment: A music recording — a song or instrumental track in its recorded form.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:AudioObject` (the file as bytes) and `schema:MusicComposition` (the abstract work). A MusicRecording is a specific recorded performance. Pair with `schema:byArtist`, `schema:inAlbum`, `schema:duration`, `schema:isrcCode`.

rdfs:label: NonRDFSource
rdfs:comment: An LDP Resource whose state is NOT RDF — typically a binary file like an image, audio, or PDF.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Resource`. Use for binary files stored in a Solid pod (photos, audio, PDF, video, plaintext, source code). The server returns the file content directly under its declared media type, not RDF. Pair with describing-resources (RDF) that reference the binary.

examples.title: A binary image stored in a pod

rdfs:label: Note
rdfs:comment: A short written work — typically a microblog post, comment, or reply.
notes: ActivityStreams short-form post: a tweet, toot, comment, status update. Use `urn:solid:Article` for longer-form essays. Pair with `urn:solid:content` (the body) and `urn:solid:attributedTo` (the author).

rdfs:label: Notification
rdfs:comment: A Linked Data Notification — a message POSTed to an inbox to inform the receiver about something.
notes: From Linked Data Notifications (LDN) and Solid notifications. POSTed to a `urn:solid:inbox` container. The payload is RDF; common shapes use ActivityStreams `as:Activity` so the same primitive carries both "a thing happened" and "please notify someone".

jsonld.urn:solid:content: Bob wants to share a file with you.

rdfs:label: Object
rdfs:comment: The base class for all ActivityStreams objects — anything that can be the subject or target of an Activity.
notes: Almost everything in ActivityStreams ultimately specializes Object — Note, Article, Image, Activity, etc. Rarely typed directly; you'll usually pick a subclass. Pair with `urn:solid:content`, `urn:solid:name`, `urn:solid:attributedTo`, and the various AS predicates.

rdfs:label: Offer
rdfs:comment: An offer to transfer some rights to an item or to provide a service — typically a price for a Product.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:Product`: an Offer is the *availability and terms* of obtaining the Product (price, currency, seller, validity window). One Product can have many Offers (different sellers, different prices, sales). Pair via `schema:itemOffered`.

rdfs:label: OnlineAccount
rdfs:comment: An account held by an Agent on some online service.
notes: Use as the value type of `urn:solid:account`. Typically described with `foaf:accountName` (the username) and `foaf:accountServiceHomepage` (the service's homepage). For a Solid pod account specifically, see `solid:Account`.

rdfs:label: OrderedCollection
rdfs:comment: An ordered collection of objects — most-recent-first by convention in ActivityPub.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Collection`. The shape used by ActivityPub inboxes and outboxes. Members are enumerated via `as:orderedItems` (or paginated via `as:first`/`as:next`); items are typically sorted reverse-chronologically.

rdfs:label: Organization
rdfs:comment: A formal organization — a company, society, institution, or other collective with structure.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Agent`: every Organization is an Agent, but not every Agent is an Organization (people, software). Use `Organization` when the actor has formal/legal structure; use `Agent` when the actor's nature is unspecified or could be a person.

rdfs:label: OrganizationalUnit
rdfs:comment: An ORG OrganizationalUnit — a part of a larger Organization (department, team, division) without independent legal status.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Organization`. Distinguishes internal divisions from legally-recognized entities (which use `urn:solid:FormalOrganization`). Pair with `urn:solid:subOrganizationOf` to point at the parent.

examples.title: An engineering team within a company

rdfs:label: PeriodOfTime
rdfs:comment: A named or bounded interval of time — a year, an era, a meeting window, a coverage period.
notes: Use as the value type of `urn:solid:temporal` for richer time-coverage metadata than a plain ISO 8601 interval string. For full temporal logic with intervals, instants, and Allen relations, use the OWL-Time vocabulary instead.

rdfs:label: Person
rdfs:comment: A human being.
notes: Use for any human individual. Prefer this over `vcard:Individual` unless vCard-specific properties are needed, and over `schema:Person` when interoperating with FOAF-based Solid data.

rdfs:label: PersonalProfileDocument
rdfs:comment: A document that describes a person — typically a FOAF or WebID profile.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Document`. The document's `foaf:primaryTopic` is the Person it describes. WebID profile documents are typically of this type. The relationship between the document and its subject Person is asymmetric: one document, one primary topic.

rdfs:label: Photo
rdfs:comment: A vCard Photo resource — a photographic image associated with a vCard.
notes: Use as @type for the value of `urn:solid:hasPhoto` when modelling the photo as a structured resource (with format, source, etc.) rather than a bare URL. For non-vCard image resources, prefer `urn:solid:Image` (FOAF) or `urn:solid:ImageObject` (schema.org).

rdfs:label: PhysicalMedium
rdfs:comment: A material or physical carrier of a resource — paper, vinyl, magnetic tape, stone tablet.
notes: Use as @type for resources representing physical media — typically referenced from `dcterms:medium`. Library and archive contexts use this to record the carrier separately from the digital format. For digital file formats, use `urn:solid:FileFormat` instead.

rdfs:label: Place
rdfs:comment: An entity that has a somewhat fixed physical extension — a city, building, landmark, room.
notes: Use for any geographic feature with a roughly stable footprint. Pair with `urn:solid:hasGeo` (or `schema:geo`) for coordinates and `urn:solid:hasAddress` for postal info. For dynamic event locations, use ActivityStreams `as:Place`.

rdfs:label: Plan
rdfs:comment: An entity describing a plan — a set of intended actions to achieve some goal.
notes: PROV subclass of `urn:solid:Entity`. A Plan is the design or recipe an Activity follows — distinct from the Activity itself (the execution). Linked to an Activity via `prov:hadPlan`, typically inside a `prov:Association`.

rdfs:label: Policy
rdfs:comment: A statement of policy applicable to the resource — terms of use, retention rules, access guidelines.
notes: Broader than `urn:solid:LicenseDocument` (which is specifically a legal grant of permissions): a Policy can be any normative document — privacy policy, retention policy, code of conduct. For machine-actionable access control on Solid pods, use the WAC vocabulary instead.

rdfs:label: PostalAddress
rdfs:comment: A structured postal address — street, locality, region, postal code, country.
notes: Use for snail-mail addresses with structured fields (`schema:streetAddress`, `schema:addressLocality`, `schema:postalCode`, `schema:addressCountry`). For vCard-flavored data, the equivalent is `vcard:Address`.

rdfs:label: PrimarySource
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV derivation typing the relation as a primary-source attribution — first-hand origin.
notes: Subclass of `prov:Derivation` typing it as primary-source attribution — eyewitness account, raw measurement, canonical document. Use the `urn:solid:hadPrimarySource` shortcut when you don't need the qualified form.

examples.title: Article based on a primary source

rdfs:label: Product
rdfs:comment: Anything that is made available for sale — a physical good, a service, or a digital item.
notes: Schema.org's commerce-anchor class. Pair with `urn:solid:Offer` (the price/availability) and `urn:solid:Review` / `urn:solid:Rating`. For non-commercial creative works, `urn:solid:CreativeWork` is the better base; Product specifically implies a market context.

rdfs:label: Project
rdfs:comment: A project — a collaborative undertaking with a goal.
notes: Use for any deliberate, goal-oriented effort — software project, research project, organizing initiative. For software projects specifically, the DOAP vocabulary (`doap:Project`) carries richer fields like repository, release, and license.

examples.title: A project with a current participant

rdfs:label: ProvenanceStatement
rdfs:comment: A statement about the provenance of a resource — its origin, custody history, transformations.
notes: Use as @type for free-form provenance documents — narrative descriptions of where a resource came from. For machine-actionable provenance graphs, prefer the PROV vocabulary (`urn:solid:Entity`, `urn:solid:Bundle`, etc.).

jsonld.urn:solid:description: Compiled from sensor readings collected by Wonderland Climate, validated against the 2026 baseline.

rdfs:label: Question
rdfs:comment: A question being asked — typically with one or more proposed answers (a poll).
notes: AS Question is both an `as:IntransitiveActivity` and an Object — it represents a poll or survey. Pair with `as:oneOf` (single-choice options) or `as:anyOf` (multi-choice). For straight Q&A without polling semantics, schema:Question + schema:Answer is more general.

rdfs:label: Quotation
rdfs:comment: A PROV Derivation that represents a quoted excerpt from another entity, with attribution.
notes: Subclass of `prov:Derivation`. Use when the new entity contains content directly lifted from another (excerpts, citations, screenshots). Distinct from `urn:solid:Revision` (substantive change to the same identity) and `prov:PrimarySource` (first-hand origin attribution).

rdfs:label: RDFSource
rdfs:comment: An LDP Resource whose state is represented as RDF — a Turtle, JSON-LD, or other RDF document.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Resource`. Use for any resource an LDP server returns as RDF — profile cards, Type Indexes, RDF data files. Containers are also `RDFSource`s (their state-as-RDF lists members). For binary files (images, videos), use `urn:solid:NonRDFSource` instead.

rdfs:label: Rating
rdfs:comment: A numeric or symbolic value expressing assessment quality — typically a star rating.
notes: Bare assessment with `schema:ratingValue` (the score), `schema:bestRating` and `schema:worstRating` (the scale). For an aggregate ("4.3 stars from 217 reviews") use `schema:AggregateRating`. Embed inside a `urn:solid:Review` via `schema:reviewRating`.

rdfs:label: Recipe
rdfs:comment: A recipe — instructions for preparing a dish, with ingredients, steps, and yield.
notes: Subclass of `schema:HowTo` (and indirectly of `urn:solid:CreativeWork`). Pair with `schema:recipeIngredient`, `schema:recipeInstructions`, `schema:recipeYield`, `schema:cookTime`, `schema:nutrition`. Heavily used by recipe sites for SEO rich results.

rdfs:label: Reject
rdfs:comment: An indication that the actor rejects the object — typically a Follow request or invitation.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. The negative counterpart of `Accept` — typically used to decline a `Follow` or invitation. The `as:object` is what's being rejected. After a Reject, the original request should not be considered active.

rdfs:label: Remove
rdfs:comment: An activity in which the actor is removing the object from the target.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. Inverse of `urn:solid:Add` — `as:object` is the thing being removed, `as:target` is the collection or container it's being removed from. The object continues to exist; only its membership in the target ends. Distinct from `Delete`, which retires the object itself.

examples.title: Remove a note from a collection

rdfs:label: Resource
rdfs:comment: An LDP Resource — any HTTP-addressable resource managed by an LDP server.
notes: The root LDP class — every Solid pod resource (file, container, RDF document) is an `ldp:Resource`. Use the more specific subclasses `urn:solid:RDFSource` (RDF documents), `urn:solid:NonRDFSource` (binary files like images), and `urn:solid:Container` (directories) when you can.

rdfs:label: Review
rdfs:comment: A review of an item — typically a Product or CreativeWork — by an author.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:CreativeWork`. A Review carries an opinion (`schema:reviewBody`), a `urn:solid:Rating`, and a pointer to the reviewed item via `schema:itemReviewed`. Distinct from `Rating`, which is the bare numeric/star value without prose.

rdfs:label: Revision
rdfs:comment: A PROV Derivation that represents a revised version of an entity — a substantive change without breaking identity continuity.
notes: Subclass of `prov:Derivation`. Use to type a derivation specifically as a revision — a v2 of a spec, a corrected dataset, an edited document. Distinct from `prov:Quotation` (excerpting) and `prov:PrimarySource` (original-source attribution).

rdfs:label: RightsStatement
rdfs:comment: A statement about the intellectual property rights held in or over a resource.
notes: Use as @type for documents stating rights — copyright notices, restriction declarations, public-domain dedications. Distinct from `urn:solid:LicenseDocument` (specifically a permission grant) and `urn:solid:Policy` (broader normative documents). The Rights Statements consortium (rightsstatements.org) provides a standardized set.

rdfs:label: Service
rdfs:comment: An ActivityStreams actor representing a service — an automated, headless software offering.
notes: AS actor type for non-interactive automated services (relays, search engines, archive bots) — distinct from `urn:solid:Application` which implies a user-facing client. Both subclass `as:Object` indirectly. The choice is descriptive, not enforced.

examples.title: An archive relay as a Service

rdfs:label: SizeOrDuration
rdfs:comment: A measured size or duration of a resource — pages, bytes, runtime, dimensions.
notes: Use as @type when modelling extent/duration as a structured resource rather than a free-form string. Typically referenced from `dcterms:extent`. For simple cases, the string form on `urn:solid:extent` or `urn:solid:duration` is sufficient.

rdfs:label: SocialMediaPosting
rdfs:comment: A post to a social-media platform — tweet, toot, status update, microblog entry.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Article`. Schema.org's social-post type — the SEO-flavored counterpart of ActivityStreams `urn:solid:Note`. For ActivityPub-flavored data, prefer `Note`; for SEO/microdata on web pages, `SocialMediaPosting`.

rdfs:label: SoftwareAgent
rdfs:comment: A piece of software acting as an agent — a script, build tool, bot, or service.
notes: PROV subclass of `urn:solid:Agent` for software actors — the right type for build pipelines, CI runs, automated curators (this loop), data-pipeline jobs. ActivityStreams equivalents are `urn:solid:Application` (interactive client) and `urn:solid:Service` (headless service); use those for ActivityPub-flavored social data.

examples.title: A curation script as a SoftwareAgent

rdfs:label: Standard
rdfs:comment: A reference point against which other resources can be evaluated or compared — a specification, schema, or policy.
notes: Use as the @type for specs, schemas, normative documents — anything resources can `dcterms:conformsTo`. RFCs, W3C Recommendations, ISO standards, JSON Schemas all qualify. Pair with `urn:solid:identifier` for a stable reference (RFC number, spec ID).

examples.title: JSON Schema declared as a Standard

rdfs:label: Tel
rdfs:comment: A vCard Tel resource — a structured telephone-number entry with type tags and value.
notes: Use as @type for the value of `urn:solid:hasTelephone` when you need typed numbers (work/home/cell/fax) or other vCard Tel sub-types. Carries `vcard:hasValue` (a `tel:` URI) and one or more sub-class types like `vcard:Voice` or `vcard:Cell`.

examples.title: vCard with a typed cell phone

rdfs:label: Tombstone
rdfs:comment: A marker for an Object that previously existed but has been deleted.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Object`. After receiving an `as:Delete`, ActivityPub servers replace the deleted object with a Tombstone — preserving the IRI so inbound references don't break, but signalling the resource is gone. Carries `as:formerType` (what it used to be) and `as:deleted` (when).

rdfs:label: TypeIndex
rdfs:comment: A registry that maps RDF classes to the locations in a Solid pod where instances of those classes are stored.
notes: The discovery mechanism Solid apps use to find where a user's data of a given type lives. A WebID typically links to one public TypeIndex (`solid:publicTypeIndex`) and one private TypeIndex (`solid:privateTypeIndex`). Each holds a set of `solid:TypeRegistration`s.

rdfs:label: TypeRegistration
rdfs:comment: An entry in a TypeIndex declaring where instances of a particular RDF class live in a Solid pod.
notes: Each TypeRegistration carries one `solid:forClass` (the RDF class) and either `solid:instance` (a single resource) or `solid:instanceContainer` (a container holding instances). Apps query the TypeIndex for registrations matching the class they need.

rdfs:label: Undo
rdfs:comment: An indication that the actor is undoing a previous activity — typically used to retract a Like or Follow.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. The `as:object` is the prior Activity being reversed (a Like to unlike, a Follow to unfollow). Distinct from `Delete`, which retires a target Object rather than reversing an Activity. The original activity remains in the historical record; Undo signals it no longer applies.

rdfs:label: Update
rdfs:comment: An activity in which the actor has updated the object.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:Activity`. The wire-level signal that an actor edited an existing object — receivers should replace their cached copy with the updated payload in `as:object`. Pair with `as:published` for when the edit happened.

rdfs:label: Usage
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV usage event — the moment an Activity used an Entity as input.
notes: Inverse-direction sibling of `urn:solid:Generation`: where Generation is "Activity → Entity" (output), Usage is "Entity → Activity" (input). Use to qualify `prov:used` with `urn:solid:atTime` and `urn:solid:hadRole`. Linked from an Activity via `prov:qualifiedUsage`.

examples.title: Qualified usage of a source file

rdfs:label: VCard
rdfs:comment: A vCard — a structured contact card holding name, email, phone, address, and other contact details.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:Person`: a VCard is the *contact record* (the data), while a Person is the *human*. One Person can have many VCards (work, personal). Pair with `urn:solid:fn`, `urn:solid:hasEmail`, `urn:solid:hasTelephone`, `urn:solid:hasAddress`.

rdfs:label: Video
rdfs:comment: A video resource — used in ActivityPub for video attachments and stand-alone video posts.
notes: ActivityStreams video type — used by PeerTube and similar federated video platforms. Distinct from `urn:solid:VideoObject` (schema.org) which carries richer SEO-friendly metadata. Pick by data flavor.

rdfs:label: VideoObject
rdfs:comment: A video file with structured metadata — duration, resolution, encoding, thumbnail.
notes: Schema.org's video type, sibling to `urn:solid:ImageObject`. Carries `schema:contentUrl`, `schema:duration`, `schema:width`/`schema:height`, `schema:thumbnailUrl`, `schema:embedUrl`. For ActivityPub-style social video posts, prefer `as:Video`.

rdfs:label: WebPage
rdfs:comment: A web page — a single page on a website, identified by its URL.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:CreativeWork` (and effectively of `urn:solid:Document`). Use when you want web-specific semantics — pair with `schema:isPartOf` pointing at the containing `WebSite`, plus `urn:solid:headline` and `urn:solid:datePublished` for SEO-friendly markup.

rdfs:label: WebSite
rdfs:comment: A website — a set of related web pages and resources at a common origin.
notes: Subclass of `urn:solid:CreativeWork`. Represents the whole site as a single resource (the value of `dcterms:isPartOf` from individual pages). Pair with `schema:potentialAction` to declare site-wide actions like search.

rdfs:label: abstract
rdfs:comment: A summary of the resource — typically one paragraph.
notes: A short summary — typical for academic papers, articles, or specs. Prefer over `urn:solid:description` when there's a distinct "abstract" section in the original. Repeat with language tags for translations.

jsonld.urn:solid:abstract: We introduce urn-solid, a curated registry of urn:solid: identifiers mapped to common RDF vocabularies, designed for LLM consumption.

rdfs:label: accessRights
rdfs:comment: Information about who can access the resource — a free-text or `dcterms:RightsStatement` description of access policy.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:rights` (general copyright/IP) and `urn:solid:license` (legal permissions): `accessRights` is specifically about WHO can access (members-only, embargoed, public, restricted to authenticated users). For Solid pod access control specifically, use the WAC vocabulary (`acl:`).

jsonld.urn:solid:accessRights: Restricted to members of the engineering team.

rdfs:label: accessURL
rdfs:comment: A URL where the resources of a DCAT Distribution can be accessed — a landing page, API entry point, or query interface.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:downloadURL`: `accessURL` is for indirect access — a landing page that explains how to obtain the data, an API root, an OAI-PMH endpoint. A Distribution must have at least one of `accessURL` or `downloadURL` per DCAT spec.

examples.title: Distribution with an API access URL

rdfs:label: account
rdfs:comment: An online account held by the subject.
notes: The value is an `OnlineAccount` resource describing the account (the service it lives on, the account name, etc.), not the bare account URL. For a Solid pod-specific notion of account ownership, see `solid:account`.

rdfs:label: accountName
rdfs:comment: The name (username, handle) of an OnlineAccount on the service that hosts it.
notes: The bare username on the hosting service — `"alice"`, not `"@alice"` or a full URL. Pair with `foaf:accountServiceHomepage` so the value is unambiguous across services.

rdfs:label: accountServiceHomepage
rdfs:comment: The homepage of the online service that hosts the account.
notes: Pair with `urn:solid:accountName` so the combination uniquely identifies the account: the value here is the service's root URL (e.g. `https://github.com/`), not the account-specific URL (`https://github.com/alice`).

rdfs:label: actedOnBehalfOf
rdfs:comment: An agent acted on behalf of another — delegation between agents.
notes: PROV's delegation relation: agent A acted with the authority of agent B. Use for bots-acting-for-users, services-on-behalf-of-orgs, ghostwriters, automated curators driven by humans. For typed delegation with role and timing, qualify via `prov:qualifiedDelegation`.

examples.title: Curation bot acting on behalf of a person

rdfs:label: additional-name
rdfs:comment: An additional or middle name of the person.
notes: vCard's middle-name field — separate from `urn:solid:givenName` and `urn:solid:familyName`. Repeat for multiple middle names. Note the hyphen in the source name is preserved. Schema.org equivalent is `schema:additionalName`.

examples.title: Person with first, middle, and last names

rdfs:label: address
rdfs:comment: The postal address of the subject.
notes: Schema.org's address predicate. The value is typically a `urn:solid:PostalAddress` resource (or a plain string for simple cases). For vCard-flavored data, use `urn:solid:hasAddress` + `vcard:Address` instead.

rdfs:label: age
rdfs:comment: The age in years of the agent.
notes: Privacy-sensitive — most modern profiles prefer `urn:solid:birthday` (which lets consumers compute current age). Value is an integer year count. For more precise temporal modelling (date of birth, life events), reach for the PROV vocabulary.

rdfs:label: altLabel
rdfs:comment: An alternative lexical label for a SKOS Concept — a synonym, abbreviation, or other equivalent name.
notes: Use for synonyms, abbreviations, common misspellings users might search for. Repeat for multiple alternates. By SKOS rule, `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, and `hiddenLabel` values for the same Concept must be pairwise disjoint within a language.

rdfs:label: alternative
rdfs:comment: An alternative title or name for the resource.
notes: For subtitles, abbreviations, working titles, translated titles. Repeat with language tags for translations. The primary title goes under `dcterms:title` (when title disambiguation is finalized) or `urn:solid:name`.

rdfs:label: alumniOf
rdfs:comment: An organization the person previously attended or worked for.
notes: Use for past educational and (loosely) professional affiliations. Repeat for multiple. Distinct from `urn:solid:worksFor` which implies *current* employment. Often pointed at a `schema:EducationalOrganization` (university, school) but any past Organization works.

rdfs:label: anniversary
rdfs:comment: An anniversary date associated with the subject — typically a wedding anniversary or other recurring date.
notes: vCard's recurring-date field — distinct from `urn:solid:birthday`/`urn:solid:bday`. ISO 8601 date. Common values are wedding anniversaries, founding dates of organizations, or other yearly remembrances. May repeat for multiple anniversaries.

rdfs:label: articleBody
rdfs:comment: The actual body of the article — its full text content.
notes: Schema.org's narrow article-text predicate, distinct from `urn:solid:headline` (the title) and `urn:solid:abstract` (the summary). For ActivityStreams Notes/Articles, `urn:solid:content` is the equivalent. May contain HTML or plain text — declare with `urn:solid:mediaType` if not HTML.

rdfs:label: atLocation
rdfs:comment: The Location at which an Activity, Entity, or Agent occurred or was situated.
notes: PROV's location-stamp predicate. Used inside qualified PROV relations (e.g. `prov:Generation`, `prov:Usage`) or directly on Activities/Agents. The value is typically a `prov:Location` (PROV's general location class) or a `urn:solid:Place`. For schema.org-flavored data, prefer `urn:solid:location`.

rdfs:label: atTime
rdfs:comment: The time at which an InstantaneousEvent occurred — for PROV Generation, Usage, Invalidation, etc.
notes: PROV's instant-event timestamp — used inside qualified PROV relations like `prov:Generation`, `prov:Usage`, `prov:Invalidation`. For activity start/end specifically, prefer `urn:solid:startedAtTime` / `urn:solid:endedAtTime`. ISO 8601.

rdfs:label: attachment
rdfs:comment: An object attached to or associated with the subject — typically images, files, or media.
notes: ActivityStreams' attachment slot — used by ActivityPub posts to carry media (images, video, polls). Repeat for multiple attachments. Each value is typically a typed object like `urn:solid:Image` or `as:Document` with a `url` and `mediaType`.

rdfs:label: attributedTo
rdfs:comment: An entity to which the object is attributed — typically the author or creator.
notes: ActivityStreams' general-purpose author/origin pointer — works for Notes, Articles, Activities, Images. The value is typically an Actor (Person, Application, Group, Service). For dcterms-style bibliographic authorship use `urn:solid:creator`; for PROV-grade attribution use `prov:wasAttributedTo`.

rdfs:label: audience
rdfs:comment: The intended audience of the object — who it is targeted at, regardless of who actually receives it.
notes: Used to declare semantic targeting (e.g. "this is for friends", "this is for the engineering team") independently of `as:to`/`as:cc` (which are wire-level addressing). The value can be an Actor, Collection, or symbolic IRI like `as:Public`.

rdfs:label: author
rdfs:comment: The author of the creative work.
notes: Schema.org's narrow authorship predicate, meant for the author of a CreativeWork. For general authorship/creation attribution use `urn:solid:creator` (dcterms); for ActivityStreams social content use `urn:solid:attributedTo`. Repeat for co-authors.

rdfs:label: available
rdfs:comment: The date or period when the resource became (or will become) available.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:issued` (formal publication): `available` is when the resource starts to be obtainable, which can differ from publication for embargoed papers, scheduled releases, or pre-orders. Can be a single date or an ISO 8601 interval.

rdfs:label: basedNear
rdfs:comment: A geographic location near where the subject is based.
notes: Intentionally fuzzy — "near", not "at" — so people can share a city or region without revealing a precise address. Value is typically a geo:SpatialThing or `schema:Place`. For a precise postal address, prefer `vcard:hasAddress` or `schema:address`.

rdfs:label: bcc
rdfs:comment: Blind carbon-copy recipients of the object — recipients hidden from other receivers.
notes: Email-style bcc: recipients receive the activity but their addresses MUST be stripped from the object before it's seen by other receivers. Use sparingly — `bcc` semantics are easily mishandled by misbehaving servers, leaking what was meant to be private.

examples.title: Note privately delivered alongside public one

rdfs:label: bday
rdfs:comment: The full date of birth of the subject (year-month-day).
notes: vCard's full birth date — `xsd:date` with year ("1990-03-14"), distinct from FOAF's `urn:solid:birthday` which is just `mm-dd` (no year). Use `bday` when you need the actual year for age calculation; use `birthday` for anniversary semantics without revealing age.

examples.title: vCard with a full birth date

rdfs:label: bibliographicCitation
rdfs:comment: A bibliographic reference for the resource — a formatted citation string.
notes: A formatted citation string as you'd see in a reference list ("Author, A. (2026). Title. Journal, vol(issue), pages."). For machine-actionable citations with structured metadata, prefer linking to a `dcterms:BibliographicResource` via `urn:solid:references` instead.

jsonld.urn:solid:bibliographicCitation: Liddell, A. (2026). On Wonderlands. Solid Journal, 1(1), 1-10.

rdfs:label: birthday
rdfs:comment: The birthday of the agent — month and day, formatted as mm-dd.
notes: FOAF format is bare `mm-dd` (no year), preserving the recurring-anniversary semantics. For a full date of birth (with year), prefer `vcard:bday` or `schema:birthDate` which take an `xsd:date`.

rdfs:label: broadMatch
rdfs:comment: A SKOS mapping asserting that a Concept in another scheme is broader than this Concept.
notes: Cross-scheme version of `urn:solid:broader`. Use across SKOS schemes when you want to say "the closest broader concept in *that* vocabulary is this one". Inverse of `urn:solid:narrowMatch`.

rdfs:label: broader
rdfs:comment: A broader (parent) SKOS Concept in a hierarchy — "category-theory broader algebra".
notes: The hierarchical-up relation in a SKOS taxonomy. Inverse of `urn:solid:narrower`. Note: SKOS treats `broader` as transitive only when used inside a single ConceptScheme — for transitive ancestor links, use `skos:broaderTransitive`. For non-hierarchical relatedness, use `urn:solid:related`.

rdfs:label: bto
rdfs:comment: Private primary recipients of the object — "to" addresses hidden from other receivers.
notes: Like `as:to` for delivery, but stripped from the object before any non-`bto` receiver sees it — use for private direct recipients you don't want exposed in the object's metadata. Same caveats as `bcc`: easily leaked by misbehaving intermediaries.

rdfs:label: byteSize
rdfs:comment: The size in bytes of a DCAT Distribution.
notes: Use to declare the file size of a Distribution so consumers can plan downloads. Integer bytes (no "MB"/"GB" suffix — use the raw number). Schema.org's `schema:contentSize` accepts free-form strings; `dcat:byteSize` is stricter.

rdfs:label: cc
rdfs:comment: Secondary public recipients of the object — visible carbon-copy addresses.
notes: Email-style cc: secondary visible recipients. ActivityPub clients typically use `cc` to add a follower collection alongside a primary `to` of `as:Public`, so a post is publicly visible AND fans out to followers' home timelines. Use `as:bcc` to reach recipients privately (not visible in the rendered object).

rdfs:label: children
rdfs:comment: A child of the person.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:parent`. Despite the plural label "children", schema.org defines this as one-child-per-statement — repeat for multiple children. Sensitive personal data; consider access control before publishing.

rdfs:label: closeMatch
rdfs:comment: A SKOS mapping asserting that two Concepts in different ConceptSchemes are similar enough to be used interchangeably in some applications.
notes: Symmetric but NOT transitive (unlike `exactMatch`) — that's the whole point: chains of close matches don't preserve enough meaning. Use when concepts overlap meaningfully but you wouldn't claim full equivalence.

rdfs:label: conformsTo
rdfs:comment: An established standard or specification to which the resource conforms.
notes: Use to declare specification compliance — e.g. a JSON-LD document conforming to a profile, an HTML page conforming to a WCAG level, a dataset conforming to a schema. Value should be the IRI of the standard, not free text. For shape conformance specifically, see SHACL/ShEx vocabularies.

examples.title: Term file conforming to the urn-solid schema

rdfs:label: contains
rdfs:comment: A resource contained by the LDP Container — i.e., a member created via HTTP POST to the container.
notes: LDP-specific containment with HTTP semantics: POSTing to the container creates a resource that's automatically a `ldp:contains` member. Unlike `urn:solid:hasPart` (a logical part-of), `contains` reflects actual server-side parent-child storage.

rdfs:label: content
rdfs:comment: The textual body of the object — its content in a natural-language string (often HTML).
notes: ActivityStreams' body field. Value is a natural-language string — by convention HTML in ActivityPub, though plain text is allowed. Accompany with `as:mediaType` if not HTML. Repeat with language tags for translations.

rdfs:label: context
rdfs:comment: The context within which the object exists or to which it relates — typically a conversation thread.
notes: ActivityPub uses `as:context` to group all messages in one conversation under a shared identifier — every reply in a thread carries the same `context` IRI, regardless of `inReplyTo` chains. Distinct from JSON-LD's `@context` (a syntactic keyword). The value is typically the IRI of the root post or a synthetic conversation resource.

rdfs:label: contributor
rdfs:comment: An entity responsible for making contributions to the resource — secondary to the principal creator.
notes: Use for editors, reviewers, translators, co-authors of secondary weight. Repeat for multiple contributors. The principal author goes under `urn:solid:creator` instead. For a richer role-aware contribution model, prefer `prov:wasAttributedTo` paired with a `prov:Role`.

rdfs:label: country-name
rdfs:comment: The country name of an Address — typically as a string.
notes: vCard's country line on an Address — typically a country name string ("United Kingdom") or an ISO 3166-1 country code ("GB"). Schema.org equivalent is `schema:addressCountry`. For a full structured country resource, use `urn:solid:Country`.

rdfs:label: created
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was created.
notes: Use ISO 8601 (`xsd:dateTime` or `xsd:date`) values. Set once at creation and never updated — for last-edit times use `urn:solid:modified`. For provenance-grade timestamps with full PROV semantics, prefer `prov:generatedAtTime`.

examples.title: A document with a creation date

rdfs:label: creator
rdfs:comment: An entity primarily responsible for making the resource.
notes: Use for the principal author or maker. Repeat to list multiple co-creators of equal weight; use `dcterms:contributor` for secondary contributors and `dcterms:publisher` for the entity that issued/distributed the resource.

rdfs:label: currentProject
rdfs:comment: A project the person is currently active on.
notes: Repeat to list multiple active projects. Move to `foaf:pastProject` when the person stops being involved. The value can be any resource — typically a `urn:solid:Project` or a `urn:solid:Document` describing the project.

examples.title: Person actively working on a project

rdfs:label: date
rdfs:comment: A point or period of time associated with the resource — generic when more specific date predicates don't apply.
notes: Generic date property — prefer the more specific `urn:solid:created`, `urn:solid:modified`, `dcterms:issued`, `dcterms:available` when the role of the date is known. Useful for legacy data or when the date's role is unclear. ISO 8601 values.

rdfs:label: dateAccepted
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was formally accepted — typically by a publisher, peer reviewer, or governing body.
notes: Common in academic publishing — captures the gap between submission, acceptance, and publication. Pair with `dcterms:dateSubmitted` and `urn:solid:issued`. ISO 8601 date.

rdfs:label: dateCreated
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was created.
notes: Schema.org's creation timestamp. Functionally equivalent to `dcterms:created` (`urn:solid:created`); pick by namespace flavor — schema.org for SEO-rich JSON-LD on web pages, dcterms for bibliographic/library data.

rdfs:label: dateModified
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was last modified.
notes: Schema.org's modification timestamp — equivalent to `dcterms:modified` (`urn:solid:modified`) and `as:updated` (`urn:solid:updated`). ISO 8601. Pair with `urn:solid:dateCreated` for the create-then-edit lifecycle.

examples.title: Article with creation and modification dates

rdfs:label: datePublished
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was published — when it became publicly available.
notes: Schema.org's publication timestamp — equivalent to `dcterms:issued` (`urn:solid:issued`) and `as:published` (`urn:solid:published`). Distinct from `urn:solid:dateCreated`: an article can be drafted in private (created) and released later (published). ISO 8601.

rdfs:label: dateSubmitted
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was formally submitted — typically to a publisher, conference, or review process.
notes: Pair with `urn:solid:dateAccepted` and `urn:solid:issued` for the full submission → review → publication timeline. Common in academic publishing, grant applications, RFC processes. ISO 8601 date.

rdfs:label: definition
rdfs:comment: A complete explanation of the intended meaning of a SKOS Concept.
notes: Use a single, dictionary-style sentence per language (multilingual via `@language`). Distinct from `urn:solid:scopeNote` (guidance on how to use the concept) and `urn:solid:description` (general dcterms description).

jsonld.urn:solid:definition: A branch of mathematics that studies abstract structures and their relationships via objects and morphisms.

rdfs:label: depiction
rdfs:comment: An image that depicts the subject.
notes: The value is the IRI of the image itself, not a document containing it. Inverse of `foaf:depicts`. For a profile photo specifically, `vcard:hasPhoto` is often more appropriate in vCard-flavored data.

rdfs:label: description
rdfs:comment: An account of the resource — a free-text description.
notes: Multi-sentence prose describing what the resource is or contains. For a one-line summary, prefer `rdfs:comment` (which is what RDF tooling usually surfaces); for a tagline, `dcterms:abstract`. Repeat with language tags for translations.

jsonld.urn:solid:description: An introduction to the urn-solid registry and how to use it.

rdfs:label: downloadURL
rdfs:comment: A direct file URL where a DCAT Distribution can be downloaded.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:accessURL`: `downloadURL` is a *direct* file link (returns the bytes), `accessURL` is any landing page or API entry point. A Distribution typically has one or the other.

rdfs:label: duration
rdfs:comment: How long the object lasts — for time-bounded objects like events, audio, or video.
notes: An `xsd:duration` value (ISO 8601 — e.g. `"PT3M30S"` for 3 minutes 30 seconds). Used on Events, audio/video objects, and any time-bounded thing. For start/end points, use `urn:solid:startTime` and `urn:solid:endTime` instead.

rdfs:label: educationLevel
rdfs:comment: The general education level the resource targets — primary, secondary, undergraduate, professional, etc.
notes: Used in educational-resources metadata to declare what level of learner the resource is suitable for. Value is typically a controlled-vocabulary term (e.g. from a `schema:DefinedTerm` set) or a free-form string when no controlled vocab applies.

rdfs:label: email
rdfs:comment: An email address for the subject, as a plain string.
notes: Schema.org's simple string-valued email predicate (`"alice@example.org"`). Distinct from `urn:solid:mbox` (FOAF, uses a `mailto:` IRI and is inverse-functional) and `urn:solid:hasEmail` (vCard, typically points at a structured vcard:Email). Use whichever matches your data source.

rdfs:label: endTime
rdfs:comment: The date and time the object ends.
notes: ISO 8601 datetime marking when an Event, Activity, or other time-bounded object ends. Pair with `urn:solid:startTime`. May be omitted for ongoing or open-ended objects. For PROV-grade activity timing, prefer `prov:endedAtTime`.

rdfs:label: endedAtTime
rdfs:comment: The time at which the activity ended.
notes: PROV-grade activity-end timestamp. Pair with `urn:solid:startedAtTime` to record execution windows. May be omitted for ongoing activities. ActivityStreams `urn:solid:endTime` is the equivalent for AS Events; pick by domain — PROV for processes, AS for calendar events.

examples.title: Build with start and end timestamps

rdfs:label: exactMatch
rdfs:comment: A SKOS mapping asserting that two Concepts in different ConceptSchemes are equivalent for retrieval purposes.
notes: Symmetric and transitive — assert sparingly because chains can produce surprising equivalences across vocabularies. For weaker similarity that doesn't claim full equivalence, prefer `urn:solid:closeMatch`. Use across SKOS schemes; within one scheme, use `urn:solid:broader`/`narrower`/`related` instead.

rdfs:label: example
rdfs:comment: An example illustrating the use of a SKOS Concept.
notes: Editorial property for cataloguers — provides a sample use of the concept. Repeat for multiple examples. Mirrors the per-term `examples` arrays on urn-solid term files (which are JSON-LD snippets, while `skos:example` is plain prose).

jsonld.urn:solid:example: The List monad in Haskell — sequences with bind/return.

rdfs:label: extent
rdfs:comment: The size or duration of the resource — pages, bytes, runtime length.
notes: Free-form size/duration string in dcterms tradition ("320 pages", "45 minutes", "2.4 MB"). For machine-readable durations specifically, prefer `urn:solid:duration` (xsd:duration). For byte counts, use `schema:contentSize` directly.

rdfs:label: family-name
rdfs:comment: The vCard family name (surname) of a person.
notes: vCard's hyphenated form of the family name — distinct from FOAF's `urn:solid:familyName` (camelCase) only by namespace. Pick `family-name` in vCard-flavored data, `familyName` in FOAF/schema-flavored data. Functionally equivalent.

rdfs:label: familyName
rdfs:comment: The family name (surname) of the person.
notes: Modern preferred form (the older `foaf:family_name` and `foaf:surname` are seen too — kept under `rdfs:seeAlso`). Pair with `foaf:givenName` for structured names. Use `urn:solid:name` for a single combined display name.

rdfs:label: firstName
rdfs:comment: The first name of a person.
notes: Older sibling of `foaf:givenName` — kept for compatibility with legacy FOAF data. New profiles should prefer `foaf:givenName` (modeled as `urn:solid:givenName` once added) and `foaf:familyName`. The semantic distinction between first/given is culture-bound; treat them as equivalent in practice.

rdfs:label: fn
rdfs:comment: Formatted name — the display name of the subject as a single string.
notes: vCard's canonical display-name property — carries the full formatted form ("Alice Liddell"), not the structured given/family fields. `urn:solid:name` is FOAF's equivalent; prefer it for non-vCard data. For structured names, use `urn:solid:givenName` + `urn:solid:familyName`.

rdfs:label: follower
rdfs:comment: An agent that follows the subject — receiving updates from them.
notes: Schema.org's reverse follower relation (their `schema:follows` is symmetric in the spec but typically used as inverse of `schema:follows`). For ActivityPub, the typical pattern is an `as:Followers` Collection at `as:followers` on the subject; for this lightweight schema.org form, just enumerate followers directly.

rdfs:label: forClass
rdfs:comment: The RDF class that a TypeRegistration is for — what type of resources live at the registered location.
notes: The discriminator for TypeIndex lookups: when an app wants to know "where do this user's photos live?", it scans the TypeIndex for a registration whose `forClass` matches the relevant class IRI (e.g. `foaf:Image`).

rdfs:label: format
rdfs:comment: The file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource.
notes: Use an IANA media type string (`text/html`, `application/ld+json`, `image/png`) for digital resources. For physical media or non-MIME formats, free-form descriptive text is acceptable. Range can also be a `dcterms:MediaType` resource for richer modelling.

rdfs:label: gender
rdfs:comment: The gender of the agent — a free-form string in FOAF tradition.
notes: Privacy-sensitive. FOAF intentionally uses a free-form string rather than an enumerated type so identity can be self-described. `schema:gender` accepts either a `GenderType` (enum) or a string; `vcard:hasGender` uses an enumerated controlled vocabulary. Use whichever matches the consumer.

rdfs:label: generatedAtTime
rdfs:comment: The time at which the entity was completely generated by some activity.
notes: PROV's precise generation timestamp — paired with `prov:wasGeneratedBy` it lets you record exactly when a build, run, or process completed. Use `urn:solid:created` for lightweight "when was this resource made" without the PROV ceremony.

rdfs:label: generator
rdfs:comment: The application that generated the object — typically a software client or service.
notes: ActivityStreams' "created with" attribution — the value is the client app (e.g. a Mastodon instance, a Solid app). Distinct from `urn:solid:wasGeneratedBy` (PROV-grade activity attribution): generator names *what software*, wasGeneratedBy names *what process run*.

examples.title: Note generated by a client app

rdfs:label: given-name
rdfs:comment: The vCard given name (first name) of a person.
notes: vCard's hyphenated form of the given name — distinct from FOAF's `urn:solid:givenName` (camelCase) only by namespace. Pick `given-name` in vCard-flavored data, `givenName` in FOAF/schema-flavored data. Functionally equivalent.

rdfs:label: givenName
rdfs:comment: The given name of a person — the personal name distinct from the family name.
notes: Modern preferred form for the personal/first name component. Pair with `urn:solid:familyName` for structured names. The older `foaf:firstName` is treated as equivalent in most consumers; prefer `givenName` for new data.

rdfs:label: hadActivity
rdfs:comment: An activity that contributed to a qualified PROV relation — typically attached to a qualified usage, generation, or derivation.
notes: Used inside qualified PROV relations (`prov:qualifiedDerivation`, `prov:qualifiedUsage`, `prov:qualifiedGeneration`) to name the specific Activity that mediated the relation. Lets you attach a Plan, Role, or timing to the connection.

examples.title: Derivation referencing the activity that produced it

rdfs:label: hadMember
rdfs:comment: An entity that was a member of a PROV Collection.
notes: PROV's collection-membership predicate (`prov:Collection` is distinct from `as:Collection` and `ldp:Container`). Use only in PROV-flavored contexts; for FOAF Group membership use `urn:solid:member`, for vCard Group use `urn:solid:hasMember`, for LDP containers use `urn:solid:contains`.

rdfs:label: hadPlan
rdfs:comment: The Plan that an Activity followed — used inside a qualified PROV Association.
notes: Used inside a `prov:Association` to point at the `urn:solid:Plan` the Agent followed when participating in the Activity. Lets PROV record "who acted, with what role, following which plan" — a build run executes a build plan; a paper review follows a review checklist.

rdfs:label: hadPrimarySource
rdfs:comment: An entity that is the primary source — the original first-hand source — for the subject entity.
notes: PROV's primary-source predicate, a specialization of `prov:wasDerivedFrom`. "Primary source" means original/first-hand — the eyewitness account, the raw measurement, the canonical document. For derivations more generally (translations, summaries, transformed datasets), `urn:solid:wasDerivedFrom` is broader.

examples.title: News article with a primary source

rdfs:label: hadRole
rdfs:comment: The role an Agent or Entity played in a qualified PROV relation — "author", "editor", "raw input", etc.
notes: Used inside qualified PROV relations to name the role taken. Distinct from `urn:solid:role` (vCard's job-title string): `hadRole` is specifically about role within an Activity or Attribution. Value is typically a `prov:Role` resource (which can be any IRI).

rdfs:label: hasAddress
rdfs:comment: A postal address associated with the subject.
notes: The value should be a `vcard:Address` (or `schema:PostalAddress`) resource carrying structured fields — `vcard:street-address`, `vcard:locality`, `vcard:postal-code`, `vcard:country-name`. For an approximate "based near" location, use `urn:solid:basedNear` instead.

rdfs:label: hasCategory
rdfs:comment: A category or tag for the vCard — describing what kind of contact it is.
notes: vCard's category/tag predicate — typical values are "work", "personal", "family", "friend". Repeat for multiple categories. For general-purpose tagging of resources (not specifically vCards), prefer `urn:solid:keywords` or `urn:solid:subject`.

examples.title: vCard categorized as a work contact

rdfs:label: hasEmail
rdfs:comment: An email address associated with the subject — typically a `mailto:` IRI.
notes: vCard's general email predicate: not inverse-functional and free of FOAF's strong identity semantics. Use `urn:solid:mbox` when the email uniquely identifies the agent (FOAF tradition). Multiple `hasEmail` values are typical (work, personal, etc.).

rdfs:label: hasFormat
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is the same intellectual content but in a different format — e.g. a PDF version of an HTML article.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:hasVersion`: same content, different file format (PDF vs HTML, MP3 vs FLAC, JSON-LD vs Turtle). Inverse is `dcterms:isFormatOf`. The format itself is described by `urn:solid:format`.

examples.title: Article available in PDF and HTML

rdfs:label: hasGender
rdfs:comment: The gender of the agent — typically referencing one of vCard's enumerated Gender values.
notes: vCard's typed gender predicate, distinct from FOAF `urn:solid:gender` (free-form string). Value is typically a `vcard:Male`, `vcard:Female`, `vcard:Other`, `vcard:None`, or a custom resource. Privacy-sensitive — collect only when needed.

rdfs:label: hasGeo
rdfs:comment: Geographic coordinates associated with the subject — typically a `geo:` IRI carrying lat/long.
notes: Use a `geo:` URI (e.g. `geo:51.5074,-0.1278`) for the value. For richer coordinate modelling with separate lat/long predicates, use `schema:GeoCoordinates` or the WGS84 `geo:` ontology.

rdfs:label: hasInstantMessage
rdfs:comment: An instant-messaging address for the subject — typically an `xmpp:`, `matrix:`, or other chat URI.
notes: vCard's general IM-address slot — covers any chat protocol via URI scheme (`xmpp:`, `matrix:`, `irc:`). Distinct from FOAF's `urn:solid:jabberID` which is XMPP-specific and a bare string. Repeat for multiple IM identities.

rdfs:label: hasKey
rdfs:comment: A cryptographic public key associated with the vCard's owner — for encryption or signature verification.
