notes: vCard's lightweight public-key pointer. Value is typically a URL of the key file (PGP, SSH, X.509). For richer key metadata (algorithm, usage, controllers), use the W3C Security Vocabulary. Repeat for multiple keys (encryption, signing, etc.).

examples.title: vCard with a PGP key URL

rdfs:label: hasLanguage
rdfs:comment: A language the subject communicates in — typically a BCP 47 language tag.
notes: vCard's communicates-in-language predicate. Functionally similar to schema's `urn:solid:knowsLanguage`; pick whichever matches your data flavor. Distinct from `urn:solid:language` (the language a *resource* is in). Value is typically a BCP 47 tag.

rdfs:label: hasLogo
rdfs:comment: A logo image associated with the vCard — typically the brand mark of an Organization.
notes: Use on Organization vCards for the brand mark. Distinct from `urn:solid:hasPhoto` (typically a person's portrait). Schema.org's equivalent is `schema:logo`. Value can be a URL or a `urn:solid:Logo` resource.

rdfs:label: hasMember
rdfs:comment: A member of the vCard Group.
notes: vCard's group-membership predicate. Distinct from `urn:solid:member` (FOAF) only by namespace; functionally the same. Use `hasMember` in vCard-flavored data, `member` in FOAF-flavored data. Repeat for multiple members.

rdfs:label: hasMemberRelation
rdfs:comment: The predicate that should be used to express membership in a DirectContainer or IndirectContainer.
notes: Used on a `DirectContainer` or `IndirectContainer` to declare which predicate the server should add when a new resource is POSTed — e.g. `schema:comment` so a new POST to a comments container produces `<post> schema:comment <new-comment>`. Alternative: `ldp:isMemberOfRelation` for the inverse direction.

examples.title: Comments container declaring its member relation

rdfs:label: hasName
rdfs:comment: A structured Name resource for the subject — separates given/family/additional/prefix/suffix into a Name object.
notes: Use when name parts need to live on a separate Name resource (e.g. for multi-script names or when the parts have their own metadata). Most data instead attaches `given-name`/`family-name`/etc. directly to the VCard. The flat-string form is `urn:solid:fn`.

rdfs:label: hasNickname
rdfs:comment: A nickname for the subject.
notes: vCard's nickname predicate — the structured equivalent of FOAF's `urn:solid:nick`. Pick `hasNickname` in vCard-flavored data, `nick` in FOAF-flavored data. Repeat for multiple nicknames.

rdfs:label: hasPart
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is included as a part of the described resource.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:isPartOf`. Use to enumerate the constituent parts of a compound resource (chapters of a book, articles in a journal issue, photos in an album). Repeat for multiple parts.

rdfs:label: hasPhoto
rdfs:comment: A photo associated with the subject — typically a portrait.
notes: vCard's photo predicate. Functionally similar to `urn:solid:img`; pick `hasPhoto` in vCard-flavored data and `img`/`depiction` in FOAF-flavored data. Multiple values are typical (gallery, alternates, sizes).

rdfs:label: hasSource
rdfs:comment: A source document for the vCard's information — typically a website or directory the data came from.
notes: vCard-specific source pointer — analogous to `dcterms:source` (`urn:solid:source`) but scoped to vCards and typed for the directory-import scenario. Useful when a contact card was scraped or auto-imported and you want to record the upstream URL.

rdfs:label: hasSubOrganization
rdfs:comment: An OrganizationalUnit (department, team, division) that is part of the parent Organization.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:subOrganizationOf`. Use to enumerate departments/units belonging to a parent. Repeat for multiple subunits.

examples.title: Company with engineering and sales units

rdfs:label: hasTelephone
rdfs:comment: A telephone number associated with the subject — typically a `tel:` IRI.
notes: Use a `tel:` URI (e.g. `tel:+44-20-1234-5678`) for the value, not a bare string. Repeat for multiple numbers. For typed numbers (work/home/mobile), the value can be a `vcard:Tel` resource carrying `vcard:hasValue` and `rdf:type` of one of the work/home/cell sub-types.

rdfs:label: hasTopConcept
rdfs:comment: A top-level (root) Concept of the SKOS ConceptScheme — has no broader concept within the scheme.
notes: Use on a ConceptScheme to enumerate its entry-point Concepts — those with no `broader` parent in the scheme. Inverse is `urn:solid:topConceptOf`. A scheme typically has a small handful of top concepts; repeat for each.

rdfs:label: hasUID
rdfs:comment: A globally unique identifier for the vCard — typically a UUID or other long-lived ID.
notes: vCard's persistent identifier — the value remains stable across edits, lets clients dedupe two card revisions for the same person. Often a `urn:uuid:`. Distinct from `urn:solid:identifier` (general-purpose secondary identifier); `hasUID` is specifically the vCard tradition's stable ID.

rdfs:label: hasURL
rdfs:comment: A URL associated with the subject — any web link, not necessarily the canonical homepage.
notes: More general than `urn:solid:homepage` — use to enumerate any URLs (social profiles, project links, work pages). Repeat for multiple. Use `homepage` when the URL is the canonical, FOAF-style identifying homepage.

rdfs:label: hasUnit
rdfs:comment: An OrganizationalUnit that is part of the parent Organization — narrower than `hasSubOrganization`.
notes: Sub-property of `urn:solid:hasSubOrganization` constrained to OrganizationalUnits (so the value is always an internal unit, not another formal organization). Use when you want type-checking on the structure.

rdfs:label: hasVersion
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is a version, edition, or adaptation of the described resource.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:isVersionOf`. Use on the abstract work to enumerate its versions/editions. Repeat for multiple versions; useful for spec families, software releases, document editions.

rdfs:label: headline
rdfs:comment: The headline of the article — a short, attention-grabbing title line.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:name` — the headline is specifically the newsroom-style top line of an article ("Local CG Founder Ships Registry"), while `name` is the generic title. Keep headlines concise (schema.org recommends ≤ 110 characters).

rdfs:label: hiddenLabel
rdfs:comment: A non-display label for a SKOS Concept — used to support search but not shown in UIs.
notes: Use for misspellings, deprecated names, slang — strings users might search for that you don't want to surface in the UI. SKOS rule: `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, and `hiddenLabel` values must be pairwise disjoint within a language for the same Concept.

rdfs:label: holds
rdfs:comment: An ORG Post (position) that an Agent currently holds within an Organization.
notes: Use to declare that a Person currently occupies a named Post (org:Post) — "holds the position of CTO". A Post is a stable, identified position that may be held by different people over time, distinct from Membership (which is the participation event itself).

rdfs:label: homepage
rdfs:comment: A homepage for the subject — a top-level page about the agent.
notes: Inverse-functional in FOAF: a homepage uniquely identifies its agent. Use the IRI of the actual page, not a description of it. For arbitrary URLs that are not the canonical homepage, prefer `schema:url` or `vcard:hasURL`.

rdfs:label: honorific-prefix
rdfs:comment: An honorific prefix preceding the person's name — Mr, Mrs, Dr, Prof, etc.
notes: vCard's honorific prefix — culture-specific. Pair with `urn:solid:honorific-suffix` for postnominals (PhD, Esq.). Schema.org equivalent is `schema:honorificPrefix`. Note the hyphen in the source name is preserved.

rdfs:label: honorific-suffix
rdfs:comment: An honorific suffix following the person's name — PhD, Esq, Jr, Sr, etc.
notes: vCard's postnominal field — degrees, generational suffixes, certifications. Pair with `urn:solid:honorific-prefix`. Schema.org equivalent is `schema:honorificSuffix`. Repeat for multiple postnominals ("PhD, FRS").

rdfs:label: icon
rdfs:comment: A small image representing the object — typically a square avatar or favicon.
notes: ActivityStreams' small-avatar slot — typically square, low-resolution, used as the visual identifier for an actor or object in lists. The value is an Image or a URL. For a full-size portrait, prefer `urn:solid:img` (FOAF) or `urn:solid:depiction`.

rdfs:label: identifier
rdfs:comment: An unambiguous reference to the resource within a given context.
notes: Use for non-URI identifiers (DOI strings, ISBN, internal IDs, UUIDs) where the resource also has a URI as its `@id`. The resource's primary identifier is its `@id`; this property records additional/secondary identifiers. Repeat to list multiple.

rdfs:label: img
rdfs:comment: An image that represents the person — typically a headshot or portrait.
notes: A sub-property of `foaf:depiction` specifically for a portrait of a person. Prefer `urn:solid:depiction` when the subject is any kind of thing or the image is not a portrait. A person may have at most one primary `img` but multiple `depiction` values.

rdfs:label: inReplyTo
rdfs:comment: An object the current object is a reply to.
notes: Use to link a reply Note (or other object) back at its parent. Forms reply threads in ActivityPub. Repeat for replies addressing multiple parents (rare). The inverse `as:replies` lives on the parent and points at a Collection of replies.

examples.title: Reply pointing at its parent note

rdfs:label: inScheme
rdfs:comment: The SKOS ConceptScheme that the Concept is a member of.
notes: Declares membership of a Concept in a ConceptScheme. A Concept may belong to multiple schemes — repeat for each. The transitive scope of `broader`/`narrower` is bounded by `inScheme` membership.

examples.title: Concept belonging to a topic taxonomy

rdfs:label: inbox
rdfs:comment: An LDN inbox — a container that accepts notifications about the resource via HTTP POST.
notes: From Linked Data Notifications (LDN). The value is a Container that accepts incoming notifications about the subject — anyone can POST to it to leave a notification (subject to access control). ActivityPub re-uses the concept under `as:inbox` (a separate but interoperable IRI).

rdfs:label: insertedContentRelation
rdfs:comment: On an IndirectContainer, the predicate the server uses to look up the actual member from the POSTed content.
notes: Used only on `urn:solid:IndirectContainer`. Tells the server: "when a resource is POSTed, look up the value of *this* predicate inside it, and use *that* as the actual member." Common pattern: an IndirectContainer for likes uses `as:actor` so the membership target is the liker, not the Like activity itself.

rdfs:label: instance
rdfs:comment: A single resource that's an instance of the class declared by the TypeRegistration.
notes: Use when the user has exactly one instance — typically a settings document or singleton. For collections of instances under a directory, use `solid:instanceContainer` instead. A single TypeRegistration may carry multiple `solid:instance` values.

examples.title: Registration for a single preferences file

rdfs:label: instanceContainer
rdfs:comment: A Container holding instances of the class declared by a TypeRegistration.
notes: Use when the user's data of a given type lives in a directory that may hold many resources (photos in `/photos/`, notes in `/notes/`). Distinct from `urn:solid:instance`, which points at a single resource. A TypeRegistration uses one or the other, not both.

rdfs:label: interest
rdfs:comment: A page about a topic of interest to the agent.
notes: The value is a page (document) representing the topic of interest, not the topic itself. For the topic resource directly (any Thing, not necessarily a Document), use `foaf:topic_interest`. Repeat to list multiple interests.

examples.title: Person interested in a Wikipedia topic

rdfs:label: invalidatedAtTime
rdfs:comment: The time at which an Entity ceased to exist.
notes: End-of-life timestamp counterpart to `urn:solid:generatedAtTime`. Records when an Entity was deleted, retracted, expired, or otherwise ceased to exist. ISO 8601. Pair with `urn:solid:wasInvalidatedBy` for the responsible Activity.

rdfs:label: isFormatOf
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is the same intellectual content of which the described resource is a different-format rendition.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:hasFormat`. Use on the alternate-format rendition to point at the canonical resource it represents in another format. Distinct from `isVersionOf` (different version/edition, not just different format).

rdfs:label: isMemberOfRelation
rdfs:comment: The predicate the server adds in the *inverse* direction when a new resource is POSTed to a DirectContainer or IndirectContainer.
notes: Inverse-direction equivalent of `ldp:hasMemberRelation`: instead of `<membershipResource> <pred> <new>`, the server adds `<new> <pred> <membershipResource>`. Use whichever direction matches your data model. A container declares one of `hasMemberRelation` or `isMemberOfRelation`, not both.

rdfs:label: isPartOf
rdfs:comment: A related resource of which the described resource is a part.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:hasPart`. Use to point at the containing resource (the book a chapter belongs to, the journal an article appears in). One value per containing whole; repeat only if the resource genuinely belongs to multiple containers.

rdfs:label: isPrimaryTopicOf
rdfs:comment: A document of which the subject is the primary topic — the inverse of `primaryTopic`.
notes: Use on a Person (or other thing) to point at the document that primarily describes them. The canonical case is a WebID: `<#me> foaf:isPrimaryTopicOf <profile-card>`. Inverse-functional in FOAF — the document uniquely identifies the subject, and vice versa.

examples.title: Person pointing to their profile document

rdfs:label: isReferencedBy
rdfs:comment: A related resource that references, cites, or otherwise points to the described resource.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:references`. Use to enumerate the inbound citations or backlinks to this resource. Repeat for multiple. Often computed by aggregators rather than asserted by the resource itself.

rdfs:label: isReplacedBy
rdfs:comment: A related resource that supplants, displaces, or supersedes the described resource.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:replaces`. Use on the older resource to point at its successor — readers can follow the chain to the current version. The schema's `supersededBy` field on a urn-solid term file is the registry-internal equivalent.

examples.title: v1 spec pointing at its successor

rdfs:label: isRequiredBy
rdfs:comment: A related resource that requires the described resource to support its function or coherence.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:requires`. Use on a dependency to enumerate downstream consumers — "this library is required by these projects". Often computed by package indexes rather than asserted by the resource itself.

examples.title: Library showing what depends on it

rdfs:label: isVersionOf
rdfs:comment: A related resource of which the described resource is a version, edition, or adaptation.
notes: Use to point at the abstract "work" the current resource is one version of. Distinct from `urn:solid:replaces` (which says "this supersedes that"); `isVersionOf` allows multiple concurrent versions of the same work without one displacing another.

examples.title: v2 spec is a version of the spec series

rdfs:label: issued
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was formally issued or published.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:created` (which is when the resource itself was made) — `issued` is when it was made publicly available. For an article drafted in private and published later, the two diverge. ISO 8601 values.

rdfs:label: jabberID
rdfs:comment: A Jabber/XMPP identifier for the Agent.
notes: Inverse-functional in FOAF — a Jabber ID uniquely identifies its owner. The value is a bare JID string like `alice@jabber.example.org`, not a `xmpp:` URI. For other instant-messaging handles, see `vcard:hasInstantMessage`.

rdfs:label: keyword
rdfs:comment: A keyword or tag describing a DCAT Dataset or Catalog — repeated for multiple keywords.
notes: DCAT prefers repeated singular `dcat:keyword` literals (one per language tag) over schema.org's comma-separated `urn:solid:keywords` string. For controlled-vocabulary topical metadata, prefer `dcat:theme` with SKOS Concepts.

rdfs:label: keywords
rdfs:comment: Keywords or tags describing the resource — typically as a comma-separated string or a list.
notes: Schema.org accepts comma-separated text, an array of strings, or `schema:DefinedTerm` references. For ActivityStreams-style hashtag/mention attachments, use `urn:solid:tag`. For broader topical metadata, `urn:solid:subject` (dcterms).

rdfs:label: knows
rdfs:comment: A person known by the subject — a directed acquaintance relationship.
notes: Asymmetric by default: A knows B does not imply B knows A. Use repeatedly to enumerate the social graph. The FOAF tradition treats this loosely — any acknowledged acquaintance counts.

rdfs:label: knowsAbout
rdfs:comment: A topic the agent has expertise in or knowledge of.
notes: Use to declare expertise ("Alice knows about category theory") rather than mere interest (`urn:solid:topic_interest`) or a page about an interest (`urn:solid:interest`). Value can be a string keyword or a SKOS Concept / topic resource. Repeat for multiple areas of expertise.

rdfs:label: knowsLanguage
rdfs:comment: A language the person speaks, writes, or otherwise communicates in.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:language` (which is the language of a *resource*) — `knowsLanguage` is the languages an *agent* communicates in. Value is typically a BCP 47 tag (`"en"`, `"de-CH"`) or a `schema:Language` resource. Repeat for multiple languages.

rdfs:label: landingPage
rdfs:comment: A web page that gives access to a DCAT Dataset, its Distributions, and additional information.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:accessURL` (a Distribution-level access link): `landingPage` is the human-facing introduction page for the whole Dataset, where browsers go for context. Distinct from FOAF `urn:solid:homepage` which is for Agent homepages.

rdfs:label: language
rdfs:comment: A language of the resource — typically a BCP 47 tag.
notes: Use BCP 47 language tags as values (`"en"`, `"en-US"`, `"de-CH"`). For multilingual resources, repeat. JSON-LD documents can also express language directly on string literals via `@language` — this property is for declaring the resource's overall language(s).

rdfs:label: lastName
rdfs:comment: The last name of a person.
notes: Older sibling of `foaf:familyName` — kept for compatibility with legacy FOAF data. New profiles should prefer `urn:solid:familyName`. The first/last vs given/family terminology is culture-bound; treat them as equivalent in practice.

rdfs:label: latitude
rdfs:comment: The latitude of a location, in decimal degrees (WGS-84).
notes: Decimal degrees, positive north of the equator. Pair with `urn:solid:longitude` on a `urn:solid:GeoCoordinates` resource. For a single shorthand `geo:` URI carrying both, use `urn:solid:hasGeo`.

rdfs:label: license
rdfs:comment: A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource.
notes: Value should be the license document's IRI (e.g. an SPDX URL or a Creative Commons license page), not free text. For unstructured rights statements use `urn:solid:rights` instead. SPDX (`https://spdx.org/licenses/MIT`) and Creative Commons URLs are the most interoperable choices.

rdfs:label: locality
rdfs:comment: The locality (city, town, village) of an Address.
notes: City/town field of a vCard Address. Pair with `urn:solid:region`, `urn:solid:postal-code`, `urn:solid:country-name`. The schema.org equivalent is `schema:addressLocality` on a `urn:solid:PostalAddress`.

rdfs:label: location
rdfs:comment: The location associated with the subject — typically a Place, address, or geographic coordinates.
notes: Generic location predicate used on Events, Actions, Organizations. The value is typically a `urn:solid:Place`, `urn:solid:PostalAddress`, or `urn:solid:GeoCoordinates`. For a person's home region (intentionally fuzzy), use `urn:solid:basedNear` (FOAF). For structured postal addresses, `urn:solid:hasAddress` (vCard).

rdfs:label: loginEndpoint
rdfs:comment: The login endpoint URL for a Solid OIDC provider.
notes: Advertised by a Solid OIDC provider, points at the URL where users can initiate authentication. Most modern Solid OIDC implementations expose this via OIDC discovery (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`) rather than via this predicate, but the term remains useful for explicit declaration.

examples.title: OIDC issuer with a login endpoint

rdfs:label: logoutEndpoint
rdfs:comment: The logout endpoint URL for a Solid OIDC provider.
notes: Counterpart to `urn:solid:loginEndpoint`. Advertised by a Solid OIDC provider as the URL where users can sign out. Most modern Solid OIDC implementations expose this via OIDC discovery (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`'s `end_session_endpoint`) rather than via this predicate.

examples.title: OIDC issuer with login and logout endpoints

rdfs:label: longitude
rdfs:comment: The longitude of a location, in decimal degrees (WGS-84).
notes: Decimal degrees, positive east of the prime meridian. Pair with `urn:solid:latitude` on a `urn:solid:GeoCoordinates` resource. For elevation as well, schema.org provides `schema:elevation`.

rdfs:label: made
rdfs:comment: A thing the agent made — the inverse of `maker`.
notes: Use on an agent to point at things they made. The inverse `urn:solid:maker` goes the other direction (work → agent). Repeat to list multiple works. For richer attribution semantics, prefer `dcterms:creator` or `prov:wasAttributedTo`.

examples.title: Person and the document they made

rdfs:label: maker
rdfs:comment: An agent that made the subject — the inverse of `made`.
notes: Use on a document or work to point at the agent that made it. The inverse `foaf:made` goes the other direction (agent → work). For richer creator semantics with role and contribution type, prefer `dcterms:creator` or `prov:wasAttributedTo`.

rdfs:label: mbox
rdfs:comment: A personal mailbox — typically a mailto: IRI.
notes: Inverse-functional in FOAF: an mbox value uniquely identifies its owner, so two agents with the same mbox are the same agent. Prefer a `mailto:` IRI as the value, not a bare string. For a plain string email, see `vcard:hasEmail` or `schema:email`.

rdfs:label: mbox_sha1sum
rdfs:comment: The SHA-1 hash of the agent's mailbox URI — a privacy-preserving inverse-functional identifier.
notes: Inverse-functional like `foaf:mbox` but doesn't reveal the actual email address. Compute the SHA-1 of the lowercased `mailto:` URI (e.g. SHA-1 of `"mailto:alice@example.org"`). Two agents with the same `mbox_sha1sum` are the same agent. Modern profiles often skip both this and `mbox` for privacy.

rdfs:label: mediaType
rdfs:comment: The MIME media type of the object — `image/png`, `text/html`, etc.
notes: ActivityStreams' content-type label — typically attached to `as:content` (to declare the format of HTML vs plain text) or to attachments. Distinct from dcterms `urn:solid:format` only by namespace; carry the same string values (IANA media types).

examples.title: Note with explicit content media type

rdfs:label: mediator
rdfs:comment: An intermediary that mediates access to or use of the resource — typically for educational or curated content.
notes: From the educational-resources tradition: a teacher who selects and uses a textbook is a `mediator`. Used to express that the resource was filtered or curated by an intermediary before reaching its `urn:solid:audience`. Niche outside library/edu contexts.

examples.title: Course material with a teacher mediator

rdfs:label: medium
rdfs:comment: The material or physical carrier of the resource.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:format`: `medium` is the physical/material carrier (paper, vinyl, parchment), `format` is the file format or media type. A book may have format `application/pdf` and medium "paperback". Library and archive metadata uses both fields when both apply.

rdfs:label: member
rdfs:comment: An agent that is a member of the group.
notes: Use to enumerate the agents that belong to a group. Repeated to list multiple members. The subject should typically be a `foaf:Group`; the value can be any Agent (Person, Organization, Group, software).

rdfs:label: memberOf
rdfs:comment: An Organization (or Group) the Agent is a member of — the inverse of `member`.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:member` (the FOAF group → member relation, also re-used by ORG). Use on the Agent to enumerate the Organizations they belong to. For role-aware membership with start/end times, attach a `urn:solid:Membership` resource instead.

rdfs:label: membershipResource
rdfs:comment: The resource that membership triples for a DirectContainer or IndirectContainer are added to.
notes: Used on `urn:solid:DirectContainer` and `urn:solid:IndirectContainer` to identify *where* membership triples land. Pair with `ldp:hasMemberRelation` (the predicate to use) and `ldp:isMemberOfRelation` (the inverse). Not used on plain `BasicContainer`s.

examples.title: DirectContainer pointing at a membership resource

rdfs:label: modified
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was last modified.
notes: Updated on every substantive edit; pair with `urn:solid:created` (set once). ISO 8601 (`xsd:dateTime` or `xsd:date`). For RDF Patch / streaming-update systems, the value typically reflects the most recent committed change.

examples.title: Document with creation and modification dates

rdfs:label: name
rdfs:comment: A name for the subject.
notes: The canonical display name. For structured names (given/family), use `foaf:givenName` and `foaf:familyName` directly until urn-solid ships equivalents.

rdfs:label: narrowMatch
rdfs:comment: A SKOS mapping asserting that a Concept in another scheme is narrower than this Concept.
notes: Cross-scheme version of `urn:solid:narrower`. Inverse of `urn:solid:broadMatch`. Use across SKOS schemes when you want to say "the closest narrower concept in *that* vocabulary is this one".

rdfs:label: narrower
rdfs:comment: A narrower (child) SKOS Concept in a hierarchy — the inverse of `broader`.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:broader`. Use to enumerate child concepts in a hierarchy. SKOS treats the relation as transitive only inside one ConceptScheme — for transitive descendants use `skos:narrowerTransitive`. Repeat for multiple children.

rdfs:label: nick
rdfs:comment: A short informal nickname for the subject — typically a chat handle or screen name.
notes: For informal handles (IRC, IM, screen names) rather than legal or display names. A subject may have many nicknames across different contexts. Use `urn:solid:name` for the canonical display name.

rdfs:label: oidcIssuer
rdfs:comment: The OpenID Connect issuer that this WebID trusts to authenticate it.
notes: The Solid OIDC trust anchor: the value is the issuer URL of the OpenID Provider whose tokens this WebID will accept. A WebID may list multiple `oidcIssuer` values for redundancy. Distinct from the older FOAF `urn:solid:openid` (a document-based pre-OIDC scheme).

examples.title: WebID with a Solid OIDC issuer

rdfs:label: openid
rdfs:comment: An OpenID identifier for the Agent — a document used to verify the Agent's identity.
notes: Inverse-functional in FOAF — an OpenID document uniquely identifies its Agent. Predates Solid OIDC; for modern Solid pods use `solid:oidcIssuer` instead, which points at the OpenID Connect issuer URL.

rdfs:label: organization-name
rdfs:comment: The name of the organization the person is affiliated with — typically the employer.
notes: vCard's quick organization-name string — useful when you only have the company name as text. For a structured affiliation, prefer `urn:solid:worksFor` pointing at a `urn:solid:Organization` resource.

rdfs:label: owner
rdfs:comment: An agent that owns the resource — typically used to declare pod ownership.
notes: Solid-specific ownership predicate — declares the WebID(s) that own a pod or resource. Pod operators can read this to determine who has full control. Distinct from `dcterms:rightsHolder` (broader copyright/IP ownership) and `urn:solid:creator` (who made it).

rdfs:label: ownerOf
rdfs:comment: A pod or resource the agent owns — the inverse of `owner`.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:owner` — declared on a WebID to enumerate the pods/resources the user owns. Useful for cross-pod ownership claims and discovery. Often co-asserted with `urn:solid:storage`.

rdfs:label: page
rdfs:comment: A document about the subject — any page that describes or discusses it.
notes: More general than `urn:solid:homepage` — any page about the subject, not just the canonical one. Repeat to list multiple. For the inverse "this page is about", see `foaf:topic` (page → subject).

examples.title: Person with a page about them

rdfs:label: parent
rdfs:comment: A parent of the person.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:children`. Repeat for multiple parents (biological, adoptive, step-). Sensitive personal data; consider access control. Distinct from `dcterms:isPartOf`/`hasPart` which encode whole-part composition rather than family relations.

rdfs:label: pastProject
rdfs:comment: A project the person is no longer active on.
notes: Use to retain history when a person's involvement ends. Repeat to list multiple. Move from `urn:solid:currentProject` here when the person stops being involved. The value can be any resource — typically a `urn:solid:Project` or a Document describing it.

rdfs:label: postal-code
rdfs:comment: The postal code (ZIP code) of an Address.
notes: vCard's postal-code field. Stored as a string because postal codes are not always numeric (UK "SW1A 1AA", Canada "K1A 0B1"). Schema.org equivalent is `schema:postalCode`.

rdfs:label: prefLabel
rdfs:comment: The preferred lexical label for a SKOS Concept — its canonical name in a given language.
notes: Exactly one `prefLabel` per language tag per Concept (SKOS integrity rule). Use language-tagged literals for multilingual vocabularies. Synonyms go under `urn:solid:altLabel`; non-display strings (typos, misspellings used for search) go under `urn:solid:hiddenLabel`.

rdfs:label: preferencesFile
rdfs:comment: A document containing the subject's private preferences.
notes: Conventionally a private document linked from the WebID profile, holding application preferences and other personal settings. Should be access-controlled (only the user can read/write). Apps discover it via the WebID and follow links from it (e.g. to the private TypeIndex).

rdfs:label: preview
rdfs:comment: An object that provides a preview of the subject — typically a thumbnail image or a snippet.
notes: ActivityStreams' general-purpose preview slot — useful for link unfurling, video posters, document covers. Distinct from `urn:solid:thumbnail` (specifically a smaller image of an Image) and `urn:solid:icon` (small avatar). The value can be any AS Object with a `urn:solid:url`.

rdfs:label: primaryTopic
rdfs:comment: The primary topic of a document — the thing the document is principally about.
notes: A document has at most one primary topic. WebID profile documents canonically have their subject Person as `foaf:primaryTopic`. The inverse is `foaf:isPrimaryTopicOf`. For documents about multiple things at equal weight, use `foaf:topic` (no primacy) instead.

rdfs:label: privateTypeIndex
rdfs:comment: The private TypeIndex for a WebID — an access-controlled registry of where personal data of each type lives.
notes: Linked from a WebID, points at the user's access-controlled TypeIndex. Used by trusted apps (after auth) to discover where personal data is stored. Pair with `urn:solid:publicTypeIndex` for the world-readable counterpart.

examples.title: WebID pointing at its private TypeIndex

rdfs:label: profileSubject
rdfs:comment: The subject (Person) that a profile document is about.
notes: Solid-specific name for the relation FOAF expresses as `foaf:primaryTopic`. Use on a profile document to point at the Person it describes. Most existing data uses `foaf:primaryTopic`; this is the modern Solid-namespaced equivalent.

rdfs:label: publicTypeIndex
rdfs:comment: The public TypeIndex for a WebID — a world-readable registry of where public data of each type lives.
notes: Linked from a WebID, points at the user's publicly-readable TypeIndex. Distinct from `urn:solid:privateTypeIndex` (access-controlled, only readable by the user and their authorized apps). Public type registrations are typically for data the user intends to share (public contact info, published content).

examples.title: WebID pointing at its public TypeIndex

rdfs:label: published
rdfs:comment: The date and time the object was published — when it went public.
notes: ActivityStreams' publication timestamp — the wall-clock time a post went out. Distinct from `urn:solid:created` (when the resource was constructed) and `urn:solid:issued` (dcterms' formal publication date). ISO 8601 `xsd:dateTime`.

rdfs:label: publisher
rdfs:comment: An entity responsible for making the resource available.
notes: The publisher distributes or hosts the resource — distinct from the creator (who made it). For self-published content the same agent may fill both roles, but model them as separate triples to keep the semantics clear.

rdfs:label: qualifiedAssociation
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV Association linked to the activity — adds role and plan to a `wasAssociatedWith` relation.
notes: Use to attach a `urn:solid:Association` that names which Plan an Agent followed and what role they took during an Activity. Pattern: keep both the unqualified `wasAssociatedWith` triple AND the qualified form.

rdfs:label: qualifiedAttribution
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV Attribution linked to the entity — adds role and timing to a `wasAttributedTo` relation.
notes: Use to attach a `urn:solid:Attribution` resource that qualifies the basic `urn:solid:wasAttributedTo` link with role (author, editor, photographer, contributor). Pattern: keep both the unqualified `wasAttributedTo` triple AND the qualified form for SPARQL convenience.

rdfs:label: qualifiedDerivation
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV Derivation linked to the entity — adds role, activity, and other context to a `wasDerivedFrom` relation.
notes: Use to attach a `urn:solid:Derivation` resource that qualifies the basic `urn:solid:wasDerivedFrom` link with role, plan, or activity. Pattern: when you need richer derivation metadata, keep both the unqualified `wasDerivedFrom` triple (for SPARQL convenience) AND the qualified form.

rdfs:label: references
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource.
notes: Use to record outbound citations or references. The inverse is `dcterms:isReferencedBy`. For richer bibliographic citations with structured metadata, prefer `dcterms:bibliographicCitation` (string) or attach a separate `dcterms:BibliographicResource`.

rdfs:label: region
rdfs:comment: The region (state, province, prefecture) of an Address.
notes: vCard's sub-national administrative region — US states, UK counties, Indian states, Japanese prefectures. Often a 2-letter code ("CA", "NY") for US data. Schema.org equivalent is `schema:addressRegion`.

rdfs:label: related
rdfs:comment: A SKOS Concept that is associatively (non-hierarchically) related to the subject Concept.
notes: Use for non-hierarchical conceptual associations — "category-theory related-to functional-programming". Symmetric in SKOS. Distinct from `urn:solid:relation` (dcterms generic relation between resources) and from `broader`/`narrower` (hierarchical).

rdfs:label: relation
rdfs:comment: A related resource — generic relation when more specific predicates don't apply.
notes: The most generic dcterms relation predicate — fallback when more specific dcterms relations (`hasPart`, `references`, `source`, `replaces`, `isVersionOf`) don't fit. Avoid when possible; the specific terms carry more semantic weight. For a similarly-loose RDF predicate, see `rdfs:seeAlso`.

rdfs:label: replaces
rdfs:comment: A related resource that the described resource supplants, displaces, or supersedes.
notes: Use to record that this resource is the new official version of an older one (a v2 spec replacing v1, a new policy replacing the prior one). The inverse is `dcterms:isReplacedBy`. For term-level supersession inside the urn-solid registry itself, the schema's `supersededBy` field on a term file is the right place.

rdfs:label: replies
rdfs:comment: A Collection of objects that are responses to the subject — the reverse of `inReplyTo`.
notes: The inverse of `urn:solid:inReplyTo`. Lives on the parent object and points at a `urn:solid:Collection` (or `OrderedCollection`) of replies. ActivityPub servers compute this by aggregating inbound `inReplyTo` from across the network.

rdfs:label: requires
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is required by the described resource to support its function or coherence.
notes: Use for hard dependencies — software that needs another library, a document that requires its referenced datasets, an API spec requiring an auth scheme. Repeat for multiple dependencies. The inverse is `dcterms:isRequiredBy`.

rdfs:label: rights
rdfs:comment: Information about rights held in and over the resource — copyright, IP, access restrictions.
notes: Free-form rights statement (e.g. "Copyright 2026 Acme Corp. All rights reserved.") or a link to a `dcterms:RightsStatement` resource. For machine-actionable permissions, use `urn:solid:license` with an SPDX or Creative Commons URL.

jsonld.urn:solid:rights: Copyright 2026 Alice Liddell. All rights reserved.

rdfs:label: rightsHolder
rdfs:comment: An agent owning or managing rights over the resource — the copyright holder, IP owner, or licensing controller.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:creator` (who made it) and `urn:solid:owner` (Solid pod ownership): `rightsHolder` is specifically about IP/copyright control. A work-for-hire has a creator (the worker) and a separate rightsHolder (the employer).

rdfs:label: role
rdfs:comment: The job role or function the person performs within an organization.
notes: vCard's role string — typically a job title or function ("Senior Engineer", "Treasurer"). For schema.org-flavored data, prefer `schema:jobTitle`. For PROV-grade role-in-Activity attribution, use `prov:hadRole`.

rdfs:label: sameAs
rdfs:comment: An external reference URL that unambiguously identifies the subject — typically a profile or canonical page on another site.
notes: Distinct from OWL's `owl:sameAs`: schema.org's `sameAs` is a soft "this is also at" reference (Wikipedia page, social profile, registry entry), without the strong identity-equivalence semantics that OWL reasoners apply. Use schema's form for everyday cross-site identity hints; use OWL's form only when you mean true identity equivalence in a reasoning sense.

rdfs:label: schoolHomepage
rdfs:comment: A homepage of a school (or other educational institution) the person attended.
notes: FOAF's lightweight "I went to that school" pointer — the value is the school's homepage URL, not a structured Organization resource. For richer educational-history data, prefer `urn:solid:alumniOf` pointing at a `schema:EducationalOrganization`. Repeat for multiple schools.

rdfs:label: scopeNote
rdfs:comment: A SKOS note clarifying the intended scope or usage of a Concept — "use this for X but not Y".
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:definition` (the meaning itself) — `scopeNote` is editorial guidance for catalogers and users about when to apply the Concept. Mirrors the disambiguation-style notes on urn-solid term files themselves.

jsonld.urn:solid:scopeNote: Use for the mathematical theory; for the database concept of "category" use the `taxonomy/category` concept instead.

rdfs:label: sha1
rdfs:comment: The SHA-1 cryptographic hash of the resource's content.
notes: Use to record content integrity for files, datasets, or releases. SHA-1 is cryptographically weakened — for new data, prefer SHA-256 (`schema:sha256` or a custom predicate). Value is the lowercase hex digest of the bytes.

rdfs:label: sibling
rdfs:comment: A sibling of the person — sharing at least one parent.
notes: Symmetric — if A is sibling of B, B is sibling of A. Use repeatedly for multiple siblings. Sensitive personal data; consider access control before publishing.

rdfs:label: source
rdfs:comment: A related resource from which the described resource is derived.
notes: Use to record the upstream origin of derived works (translations, adaptations, summaries, scraped data). For PROV-grade derivation chains with role and timing, prefer `prov:wasDerivedFrom`. Repeat to list multiple sources.

rdfs:label: spatial
rdfs:comment: The spatial coverage of the resource — what places it is about or applies to.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:location` (where the resource itself *is*) — `spatial` is the geographic *subject* of the resource (a study about Wales, a dataset covering the Pacific). Value is typically a `dcterms:Location` or a `urn:solid:Place`. Pair with `urn:solid:temporal` for the time dimension.

rdfs:label: spouse
rdfs:comment: The person to whom the subject is married.
notes: Symmetric in practice — if A is the spouse of B, B is the spouse of A. Sensitive personal data; consider access control before publishing. For other family relations, schema.org provides `parent`, `children`, `sibling`, `relatedTo`.

rdfs:label: startTime
rdfs:comment: The date and time the object begins.
notes: ISO 8601 datetime marking when an Event, Activity, or other time-bounded object begins. Pair with `urn:solid:endTime` (or `urn:solid:duration`). For PROV-grade activity timing, prefer `prov:startedAtTime`.

examples.title: Event with start and end times

rdfs:label: startedAtTime
rdfs:comment: The time at which the activity started.
notes: PROV-grade activity-start timestamp. Use on a `prov:Activity` to record when execution began. ActivityStreams `urn:solid:startTime` is the equivalent for AS Events; pick by domain — PROV for processes, AS for calendar events.

rdfs:label: status
rdfs:comment: A free-form status string for the agent — e.g. "online", "away", or a custom message.
notes: FOAF's lightweight presence/status field — IM-style "away", "busy", or a free-form message ("writing the registry"). For ActivityPub-style profile bios, `as:summary` on the actor is more common today.

rdfs:label: storage
rdfs:comment: The root of a personal data store (Solid pod) for the subject.
notes: From the PIM space vocabulary. The value is the root URL of the user's pod (a Container). A WebID may list multiple `pim:storage` values when the user has multiple pods. Apps use this to discover where to read/write data on behalf of the user.

examples.title: WebID with a pod storage root

rdfs:label: street-address
rdfs:comment: The street address of an Address — number, street name, unit.
notes: vCard's street-address line. Note the hyphen in the source name is preserved. Pair with `urn:solid:locality`, `urn:solid:region`, `urn:solid:postal-code`, `urn:solid:country-name` on a `vcard:Address`. For a schema.org-flavored address, use `schema:streetAddress` on a `urn:solid:PostalAddress`.

rdfs:label: subOrganizationOf
rdfs:comment: The parent Organization that this OrganizationalUnit is part of — the inverse of `hasSubOrganization`.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:hasSubOrganization`. Use on a unit to point at its parent — useful for traversal up an org chart. Typically declared once (a unit has one parent), but ORG allows multiple parents for matrix structures.

examples.title: Engineering team pointing at parent company

rdfs:label: subject
rdfs:comment: A topic of the resource — typically expressed as keywords, key phrases, or controlled-vocabulary terms.
notes: Use repeatedly to enumerate subjects. Values can be string keywords, but a SKOS Concept or controlled-vocabulary term is preferred for interoperability. For "the principal thing this document is about", `urn:solid:primaryTopic` is more specific.

rdfs:label: summary
rdfs:comment: A natural-language summary of the object — typically shorter than its `content`.
notes: ActivityStreams' short-form digest — in Mastodon and other fediverse clients this is the content-warning / spoiler-text field. Pair with `urn:solid:content` for the full body. For long-form bibliographic abstracts, prefer `urn:solid:abstract`; for generic resource descriptions, `urn:solid:description`.

rdfs:label: tableOfContents
rdfs:comment: A list of subunits of the resource — chapters, sections, parts.
notes: Free-form text or list — typically a serialized TOC. For a structured part-of relation pointing at separate resources for each subunit, prefer `urn:solid:hasPart` (then each part has its own resource and metadata).

examples.title: Book with a table of contents

jsonld.urn:solid:tableOfContents: Ch 1: Down the Rabbit-Hole; Ch 2: The Pool of Tears; Ch 3: A Caucus-Race; ...

rdfs:label: tag
rdfs:comment: An object that is part of the private secondary audience of the subject — typically a hashtag or @mention.
notes: ActivityStreams' inline-mention slot — used by ActivityPub posts to attach `as:Hashtag` or `as:Mention` references that surface in the body. Repeat to list multiple tags. Distinct from `urn:solid:subject` (broader topical metadata) and `urn:solid:audience` (intended recipients).

rdfs:label: target
rdfs:comment: The target of the activity — the indirect object of the action.
notes: Where `as:object` is the direct object of an Activity, `as:target` is the indirect object — the destination, recipient, or container. For `as:Add`, `as:Move`, `as:Remove`: the collection items are added to / moved into / removed from. For `as:Like`: rarely used (object is enough).

examples.title: Add a note to a collection

rdfs:label: telephone
rdfs:comment: A telephone number for the subject — typically as a plain string.
notes: Schema.org's simple string-valued phone predicate ("+44-20-1234-5678"). Distinct from `urn:solid:hasTelephone` (vCard, uses a `tel:` URI for stricter parsing). Use whichever matches your data flavor.

rdfs:label: temporal
rdfs:comment: The temporal coverage of the resource — what time period it is about or applies to.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:date`/`urn:solid:created` (when the resource was made) — `temporal` is the time period the resource is *about* (a 19th-century history dataset, a Q1-2026 financial report). Value is typically a `dcterms:PeriodOfTime` or an ISO 8601 interval string. Pair with `urn:solid:spatial`.

rdfs:label: thumbnail
rdfs:comment: A thumbnail rendering of the image — a smaller version for previews.
notes: Use on a full-size image to point at a smaller preview rendition. Both subject and object should be `urn:solid:Image`. For richer image-object metadata (width, height, content URL), schema:ImageObject + schema:thumbnail carry more fields.

rdfs:label: to
rdfs:comment: The primary recipients of the object — the wire-level "send to" addresses.
notes: ActivityPub's primary delivery list — receivers in `to` are visible recipients and the activity is delivered to their inboxes. Use the symbolic IRI `https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams#Public` to make a post world-readable. For semantic targeting ("intended for friends"), use `urn:solid:audience` instead.

rdfs:label: topConceptOf
rdfs:comment: The SKOS ConceptScheme of which the Concept is a top-level entry-point — the inverse of `hasTopConcept`.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:hasTopConcept`. Use on the Concept side when you want top-concept membership declared without editing the ConceptScheme. Implies `inScheme` membership for the same scheme.

rdfs:label: topic
rdfs:comment: A thing the document is about — the inverse of `page`.
notes: A document can have many `topic`s with no implied primacy. Use `urn:solid:primaryTopic` when one topic is the principal subject (one per document). The inverse `urn:solid:page` goes from subject → document.

rdfs:label: topic_interest
rdfs:comment: A thing the agent is interested in — points at the resource itself, not at a page about it.
notes: Use when the interest target is itself a resource (a Person, Organization, Project, concept). For "a page about something I'm interested in", use `urn:solid:interest`. Note the underscore in the source name is preserved.

rdfs:label: unitOf
rdfs:comment: The parent Organization that this OrganizationalUnit belongs to — inverse of `hasUnit`.
notes: Sub-property of `urn:solid:subOrganizationOf` constrained to point at the parent of an OrganizationalUnit. Inverse of `urn:solid:hasUnit`. Functionally equivalent to `subOrganizationOf` for OrganizationalUnit subjects.

rdfs:label: updated
rdfs:comment: The date and time the object was last updated.
notes: ActivityStreams' last-edit timestamp. Functionally equivalent to `dcterms:modified` (`urn:solid:modified`), but stays in the AS namespace for ActivityPub-flavored data. ISO 8601 `xsd:dateTime`. Pair with `urn:solid:published` (first-published time).

examples.title: Note with publication and update timestamps

rdfs:label: used
rdfs:comment: An entity used by the activity — an input or dependency that existed before the activity started.
notes: PROV's input pointer: the activity consumed or referenced the entity. Pair with `prov:wasGeneratedBy` on the output side to form a full input-activity-output chain. For typed usage with roles or timing, qualify with `prov:qualifiedUsage`.

rdfs:label: valid
rdfs:comment: The date or period of validity of the resource — when it should be considered current and applicable.
notes: Use for time-bounded resources — coupons, certificates, regulations, embargoed reports. Value is typically an ISO 8601 interval. Distinct from `urn:solid:available` (when it became obtainable) and `urn:solid:issued` (when it was published).

rdfs:label: wasAssociatedWith
rdfs:comment: An agent that had a role or responsibility in the activity — performed it, oversaw it, or was implicated in it.
notes: PROV agent-to-Activity relation — distinct from `wasAttributedTo` (which links an Entity to its responsible Agent). Use `wasAssociatedWith` for who ran the build, who reviewed the change, who triggered the pipeline. Qualify via `prov:qualifiedAssociation` to add a role and a Plan.

examples.title: Build associated with a software agent

rdfs:label: wasAttributedTo
rdfs:comment: An agent to which the entity is attributed — without claiming the agent performed any specific action.
notes: PROV's lightweight "this is associated with that agent" relation — weaker than `prov:wasGeneratedBy` (which requires a specific Activity). For richer attribution with a role, qualify via `prov:qualifiedAttribution` and a `prov:Attribution` resource.

rdfs:label: wasDerivedFrom
rdfs:comment: An entity from which the subject entity was derived — a precursor or input.
notes: Use to record the upstream entity a derived work descends from — translations, summaries, transformed datasets. Repeat to list multiple sources. For typed derivation (revision, quotation, primary-source), pair with `prov:qualifiedDerivation` and a `prov:Derivation` resource.

rdfs:label: wasGeneratedBy
rdfs:comment: The PROV activity that generated the entity — the production event responsible for its existence.
notes: PROV-grade pointer from an entity (the result) at the activity (the process). Pair with `prov:generatedAtTime` for the timestamp. For lighter-weight "this was created" semantics without a separate Activity resource, `urn:solid:created` (a date) is sufficient.

examples.title: Document generated by a build run

rdfs:label: wasInformedBy
rdfs:comment: An activity exchanged information with the prior activity — without naming the entity that flowed between them.
notes: PROV's lightweight "this activity follows that one" relation — used when you want to record temporal/causal ordering between activities without modelling the intermediate Entity. For full traceability, prefer chaining `urn:solid:used` and `urn:solid:wasGeneratedBy` through explicit Entities.

examples.title: Build informed by previous test run

rdfs:label: wasInvalidatedBy
rdfs:comment: The PROV Activity that invalidated (deleted, retracted, expired) the Entity.
notes: PROV's invalidation pointer — the inverse-in-time of `prov:wasGeneratedBy`. Records that an Entity ceased to exist at a particular Activity. Pair with `prov:invalidatedAtTime` for the timestamp. ActivityStreams' lighter equivalent for social data is `as:Tombstone`.

rdfs:label: weblog
rdfs:comment: A weblog (blog) of the subject — the document the agent publishes posts to.
notes: Points at the blog as a whole, not at an individual post. An agent may have multiple weblogs (personal, work, project-specific). Use `urn:solid:homepage` for the main page about the agent rather than their writing feed.

rdfs:label: workplaceHomepage
rdfs:comment: A homepage of an organization the person works for.
notes: FOAF's lightweight "I work at that place" pointer — the value is the employer's homepage URL, not a structured Organization resource. For richer employment metadata, prefer `urn:solid:worksFor` pointing at a `urn:solid:Organization`. Repeat for multiple workplaces.

rdfs:label: worksFor
rdfs:comment: An organization the person currently works for.
notes: Use for current employment relationships. For past employers, use `schema:alumniOf`. For looser group affiliations (clubs, mailing lists, project contributors), `urn:solid:member` is more apt — `worksFor` implies an employment-like commitment.
